title: Three in Beasley NBA Betting Case to Plead Guilty, Prosecutor Says
summary: Three of the five remaining defendants in the federal case accusing former NBA guard Malik Beasley of fixing his own stat lines for bettors intend to plead guilty, a prosecutor told a Brooklyn judge on Wednesday. Beasley’s lawyer says he has no plans to plead. Beasley Holds Out as Others Move Toward...
content:
Three of the five remaining defendants in the federal case accusing former NBA guard Malik Beasley of fixing his own stat lines for bettors intend to plead guilty, a prosecutor told a Brooklyn judge on Wednesday. Beasley’s lawyer says he has no plans to plead.

Key Takeaways

  • A prosecutor told the court three of the five remaining defendants intend to plead guilty; two have not.
  • Co-defendant William Brown has already pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud conspiracy.
  • Beasley is accused of altering his play for bets in four 2023-24 Bucks games; the trial is set for May 17, 2027.

Beasley Holds Out as Others Move Toward Pleas

Per The Athletic, Assistant U.S. Attorney David Berman told Judge LaShann DeArcy Hall that the government believes three of the five remaining defendants will plead guilty, while the other two have not yet entertained plea deals. It was not disclosed which defendants intend to plead. Beasley and his co-defendant Ed Davis, a former NBA player, both attended the hearing.

Steve Haney, an attorney for Beasley, told The Athletic that his client does not intend to plead guilty as of now and is still reviewing discovery and possible defenses. Lawyers for Davis, his former agent Paolo Zamorano, Ernesto Plascencia, and Robert Gorodetsky did not respond or would not say whether their clients plan to plead. A sixth defendant, William Brown, has already pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, The Athletic reported. If the case makes it to trial, then it is set to begin May 17, 2027.

The six men were charged in an indictment unsealed on June 29 with wire fraud conspiracy, bribery in sporting contests, honest services wire fraud conspiracy, and money laundering conspiracy.

Prosecutors allege that Beasley, then with the Milwaukee Bucks in the 2023-24 season, agreed with Davis in advance to underperform or overperform on specific statistics in exchange for reductions in gambling debts he owed Davis, and that the others used that information to place wagers totaling hundreds of thousands of dollars through multiple betting operators. U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. said the defendants “turned professional basketball into a criminal betting operation.” Each faces up to 20 years in prison on each wire fraud and money-laundering conspiracy count, and up to five years on the sports-bribery count.

According to The Athletic’s account of the indictment, the alleged fixes covered four Bucks games in 2024: against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Jan. 26, the Charlotte Hornets on Feb. 27, the Los Angeles Clippers on March 10, and the Brooklyn Nets on March 21. Most wagers were on Beasley falling short of statistical thresholds, though he did not manage to stay under his rebounding line against the Nets.

Judge Hall is also handling the case against former Miami Heat guard Terry Rozier over an alleged bribe to exit a game early. The bets at issue in both were player props, or wagers on an individual’s statistics, which prediction markets now list as well: Kalshi lists NBA player points and rebounds markets. In comments to the CFTC this spring, players’ unions for the NFL, MLB, NBA, NHL, and MLS urged the agency to prohibit contracts based on a “negative” outcome, including so-called under bets.

title: MSCI adopts index exclusion rules that could oust Strategy
summary: Strategy, Metaplanet and Upexi were previously identified for deletion under the methodology, with MSCI set to announce its final list on Nov. 11.
content:
Index provider MSCI has adopted new rules that could lead to Strategy, Metaplanet and Upexi being removed from its global indexes, while leaving several other crypto treasury companies facing potential exclusion. 

MSCI said Thursday it will adopt a methodology proposed in August that would make “non-operating companies” ineligible for inclusion in the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes. 

MSCI previously identified Strategy (MSTR) among the companies that would be deleted from the indexes under the “non-operating companies methodology.” Sharplink, Inc (SBET), Ton Strategy Company (TONX), Solana Company (HSDT) and DeFi Development Corp. (DFDV) are among companies that would be put on a “watchlist” for potential removal. 

Removal could force funds tracking MSCI indexes to sell the affected companies’ shares, potentially putting pressure on stock prices and reducing passive investment demand.

“It removes a company from the default portfolios of tens of millions of people who never chose to remove it,” said Conner Brown, executive director of the Bitcoin Policy Institute in September, who was describing the consequences of broad-market index exclusion, with Strategy as the example. 

Related: Strategy adds 250 Bitcoin as holdings reach 848,250 BTC 

Under the new methodology, MSCI will assess companies based on their operating assets and five financial ratios. Companies failing at least four of the five tests could be deemed ineligible. Existing companies in the index must generally fail the screening process over two annual reporting periods before removal. 

The final list of companies to be removed will be released on Nov. 11 and will take effect on Nov. 30, 2026, according to MSCI. 

JPMorgan analysts previously estimated that Strategy’s exclusion from MSCI indexes could trigger roughly $2.8 billion in selling. That estimate concerned MSCI’s earlier digital asset proposal, rather than the rules adopted Thursday.

In August, Strategy opposed the changes but also played down the potential disruption, saying funds tracking MSCI’s Global Investable Market Indexes hold approximately 13 million shares, representing 3.1% of its basic shares outstanding. The company said those holdings amount to less than one day’s trading volume.

title: Solana Breaches China’s Crypto Wall With New Shanghai Office
summary: The establishment of a new Solana Foundation office in one of Shanghai’s highest commercial buildings has drawn out criticism from industry leaders, who wonder how China, with its historic anti-crypto stance, allowed a top-ten cryptocurrency to set up shop in the country. Solana’s New Office in Chin...
content:
The establishment of a new Solana Foundation office in one of Shanghai’s highest commercial buildings has drawn out criticism from industry leaders, who wonder how China, with its historic anti-crypto stance, allowed a top-ten cryptocurrency to set up shop in the country.

Key Takeaways

  • Solana opened a Shanghai office and hosted landmark city light shows despite China’s strict crypto bans.
  • By focusing on tech and AI over token speculation, Solana secured local state-backed builder partnerships.
  • Establishing an early footprint in China gives Solana a major advantage if Beijing eases crypto restrictions.

Solana’s New Office in China Draws Scrutiny From Broader Crypto Ecosystem

Solana seems to have bypassed China’s Great Crypto Wall to set up a commercial office high in Shanghai’s commercial district.

The office, in the Shanghai Tower in the Lujiazui financial district, was first shown in a video shared by Vibhu Norby, Chief Product Officer of the Solana Foundation, surprising high-level cryptocurrency executives, who wondered how a top-ten crypto firm could have entered China with its historical anti-digital-asset policies, with the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) doubling down on its position earlier this year.

The Solana Foundation also promoted its brand by organizing a light show with the word SOLANA and the cryptocurrency’s colors on the giant curtain wall of the Citibank Tower in Lujiazui.

“It’s amazing to see that Solana was able to advertise and even get an office in China. BNB Chain was not able to do this, so far. Hopefully, what’s good for one industry player is also good for the rest,” declared Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, who was surprised by this event.

While social media sources have claimed that videos of the Solana light show have been taken down on Douyin, the Chinese TikTok, with “SOL Shanghai” searches being classified as a violation, others have framed this experience from a different perspective.

Local sources indicated that this development was part of a push to enter China as a tech company, and not as a cryptocurrency organization. Techflow argues that by March, Solana had already partnered with Shanghai Hongqiao Alibaba Center to launch the “Shanghai Builder Station,” receiving endorsement from the government.

Solana is also kicking off the Solana Accelerate China event across four cities, including Shanghai, Hangzhou, Shenzhen, and Beijing. The event agenda features themes like artificial intelligence (AI), Robotics, physical AI, emerging markets, and local business development, avoiding subjects directly linked to speculation and the SOL token, as argued by Techflow.

So, this means the Solana Foundation has opted to enter the Chinese space with a holistic approach, and maybe wait and see whether China changes its current crypto policy, playing the long game.

It remains to be seen whether this will actually happen. But if it does, Solana will have a leg up compared to other networks, having already established a presence in the Chinese ecosystem.

title: Blackrock Boss Larry Fink Sounds Recession Alarm Over AI Data Center Shutdowns
summary: Blackrock CEO Larry Fink is sounding the recession alarm over proposals to halt new data center construction, warning that America’s artificial intelligence (AI) investment boom has become too important to interrupt. His comments arrive as communities and lawmakers challenge the industry’s electrici...
content:
Blackrock CEO Larry Fink is sounding the recession alarm over proposals to halt new data center construction, warning that America’s artificial intelligence (AI) investment boom has become too important to interrupt. His comments arrive as communities and lawmakers challenge the industry’s electricity consumption, water demands, and rising utility costs. Yet Blackrock is hardly a bystander, with an AI infrastructure partnership targeting as much as $100 billion in investment.

Key Takeaways

  • Larry Fink warns that halting data center construction risks pushing the U.S. economy into recession.
  • Blackrock’s AI infrastructure partnership targets up to $100 billion in investment.
  • Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez want a federal pause until stronger consumer and environmental safeguards exist.

Blackrock’s Larry Fink Warns Data Center Freeze Could Push U.S. Into Recession

America’s artificial intelligence (AI) boom has become so deeply woven into the economy that stopping new data center construction could help tip the country into recession, according to Blackrock CEO Larry Fink. The warning comes as politicians, environmental organizations and frustrated residents push for restrictions on enormous computing facilities consuming electricity and water.

But there’s another wrinkle. Blackrock itself is helping bankroll the very infrastructure at the center of the controversy, including a partnership targeting up to $100 billion in investment. With trillions in future AI spending at stake, the fight over who foots the bill is heating up.

Fink Sounds Recession Alarm as Data Center Opposition Grows

Speaking to CNBC on Wednesday, Oct. 14, following Blackrock’s third-quarter earnings report, Fink delivered a stark assessment of what a nationwide construction freeze might mean. “If we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession,” Fink told CNBC, according to a report by CNBC reporter Paulina Likos.

“So much of our economy is based on the buildout of this capex,” he added, referring to capital expenditures supporting artificial intelligence infrastructure. Fink further acknowledged public concerns surrounding the construction boom but argued that “most of it is on misinformation.” The Blackrock chief executive insisted:

“Data centers are not the problem. They’re creating more new jobs than ever before.”

His remarks arrive as opposition gathers momentum ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections. Communities are questioning whether the economic benefits justify higher electricity bills, water requirements and environmental disruption.

Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez Push for Construction Pause

Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., are among the prominent lawmakers advocating a federal moratorium on certain AI data center projects until stronger consumer, labor and environmental protections are established. Environmental organizations, including Food & Water Watch, have rallied hundreds of groups behind calls for restrictions.

Their argument is straightforward. Communities shouldn’t have to absorb rising infrastructure costs while technology companies race to expand computing capacity. New York has already imposed a temporary statewide pause on certain large AI data centers, while other jurisdictions are considering restrictions. The proposals generally target new construction or major expansions rather than shutting down operating facilities. Supporters describe them as opportunities to establish rules before approving additional projects.

Blackrock Has Billions Riding on AI Infrastructure

Fink’s warning carries another dimension because Blackrock has considerable financial interests tied to continued AI development. Through its AI Infrastructure Partnership with Microsoft, MGX, and other investors, Blackrock is participating in an initiative designed to mobilize $30 billion in equity and potentially $100 billion, including debt. The consortium’s roughly $40 billion acquisition of Aligned Data Centers illustrates the scale of that commitment.

During the CNBC interview with Jim Cramer, Fink described growing demand for financing throughout the American economy. “Well, I think some of that is some of our success. I mean, we are seeing demand for capital in all different segments of the economy,” he explained.

“I know everything related to AI and data centers is sexy and appealing. And we want to talk about it. But more and more organizations are coming to the capital markets. Blackrock is at the center point of those conversations,” Fink said.

A Trillion-Dollar Spending Boom Meets Political Resistance

Wall Street projections cited by CNBC suggest annual AI capital expenditures could exceed $1 trillion in 2027, with cumulative investment topping $5 trillion by 2030. Those forecasts help explain why Fink is sounding the alarm. Data center construction supports demand for electrical equipment, construction labor, energy infrastructure, semiconductors and financing.

At the same time, AI supporters argue that claims about artificial intelligence’s water consumption are often exaggerated. Early estimates suggesting a single ChatGPT response uses half a liter of water included both cooling systems and electricity production, often using worst-case scenarios. Newer measurements tell a different story.

Google’s AI team reports that a typical Gemini text prompt uses just 0.26 milliliters, roughly five drops. AI proponents also note that data centers account for a small fraction of America’s freshwater consumption, while newer cooling systems increasingly recycle water or use outside air.

They compare AI’s water demands with golf courses, lawn irrigation, and agricultural systems, arguing that consumption is relatively modest, although local water shortages remain a legitimate concern. If AI protests and moratoriums continue to gain traction, Fink sees a recession risk in restricting development. Opponents see financial and environmental risks in allowing expansion without stronger safeguards.

For Blackrock, the stakes include both the broader economy and its own infrastructure investments. For communities debating whether another data center belongs in their backyard, the question is considerably more immediate. Who gets the economic rewards, and who pays for the power?

title: Australia releases draft bill to adopt OECD crypto tax reporting framework
summary: Australia is among 77 jurisdictions committed to adopting CARF, with its first international exchanges of crypto tax data expected in 2028.
content:
Australia has released draft legislation that would enable the automatic exchange of crypto tax information between countries. 

The draft bill, Treasury Laws Amendment Bill 2026: Tax information reporting, is open to comment until Oct. 28. It would establish a framework to implement the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) in Australian law and introduce a domestic crypto reporting regime, according to the Australian Treasury. 

Australia first signaled its intention to implement CARF in November 2023 and consulted on its proposed approach in late 2024. The government subsequently announced plans to implement both CARF and a domestic crypto reporting regime in its 2025–26 Mid-Year Economic and Fiscal Outlook, with international exchanges of crypto tax information expected to begin in 2028.

The OECD approved CARF in August 2022 to address tax evasion risks arising from the growth of crypto assets.

Related: Australia seeks feedback on crypto platform rules ahead of 2027 rollout

title: Multiliquid Raises $8M to Challenge Slow Settlement on Wall Street
summary: Multiliquid has secured $8 million in total funding after closing a seed round led by Polychain, with backing from Circle Ventures and five other investment firms. Developed by Uniform Labs, the platform addresses a stubborn problem in tokenized finance: Assets representing Treasuries, money market ...
content:
Multiliquid has secured $8 million in total funding after closing a seed round led by Polychain, with backing from Circle Ventures and five other investment firms. Developed by Uniform Labs, the platform addresses a stubborn problem in tokenized finance: Assets representing Treasuries, money market funds and private credit can trade on blockchains, yet converting them into spendable stablecoins can still take days.

Key Takeaways

  • Multiliquid’s total funding reached $8 million after a seed round led by Polychain.
  • Circle Ventures joined five other investors backing Multiliquid’s institutional liquidity platform.
  • Multiliquid aims to make exchanges between tokenized investments and stablecoins available around the clock.

Multiliquid Reaches $8 Million in Funding as Polychain Backs Tokenized Asset Liquidity

Tokenized assets promise around-the-clock finance, but there’s a catch. Even when traditional finance (TradFi) investments live on a blockchain, turning them into usable cash can still take days. Multiliquid wants to eliminate that waiting period, and investors are putting money behind the idea.

On Thursday, Oct. 15, Uniform Labs announced that its institutional liquidity platform had closed a seed round led by Polychain, bringing total funding to $8 million, with participation from Circle Ventures and five other investment firms.

Polychain Leads Funding for Institutional Liquidity

The financing attracted Strobe Ventures, CMT Digital, Metalayer Ventures, Generative Ventures, and Circle Ventures alongside lead investor Polychain. The company did not disclose the seed round’s individual size. Multiliquid is designed to let institutions exchange tokenized financial assets for stablecoins through a single blockchain transaction.

This is in contrast to the current method of navigating conventional TradFi redemption processes that can stretch across several business days. The protocol supports tokenized funds from asset managers including Wellington Management, Vaneck, Janus Henderson and Fasanara, alongside stablecoins such as USDC.

Tokenized Assets Meet a Familiar Wall Street Problem

The underlying problem isn’t necessarily creating digital versions of traditional investments. It’s making those investments liquid enough to move between markets without tying up capital. The distinction has become increasingly important as institutions explore tokenized Treasuries, money market funds and private credit.

“Tokenization only matters if the assets are actually liquid,” Multiliquid founder and CEO Will Beeson remarked.

Stablecoin Rules Add Another Dimension

The GENIUS Act prohibits payment stablecoin issuers from paying holders interest or yield directly, creating a distinction between transactional stablecoins and yield-bearing tokenized investments. Multiliquid aims to bridge those two categories, allowing institutions to shift capital between investments and stablecoins without waiting for conventional settlement windows.

Polychain founder Olaf Carlson-Wee described liquidity as the remaining bottleneck for tokenized assets. The larger question is whether blockchain-based settlement can deliver the liquidity institutions expect from traditional capital markets, rather than simply digitizing assets that remain difficult to redeem.

title: Brooklyn DA Pulls the Plug on Crypto Scam Network
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Brooklyn DA Pulls the Plug on Crypto Scam Network
112 servers and 241 fake sites knocked offline in one of the largest cyber takedowns ever by a local prosecutor.
This post Brooklyn DA Pulls the Plug on Crypto Scam Network first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew...
content:
The Brooklyn District Attorney’s office has dismantled the online backbone of a multinational cryptocurrency scam that drained tens of millions of dollars from Russian-speaking victims across the U.S.

Working with the FBI, investigators executed search warrants across three time zones in a matter of hours and seized or disrupted 241 scam domains and more than 100 cloud servers hosted by Eastern European and American companies. The servers held the scammers’ victim data, site content and operating software, according to a Wednesday statement. 

“Our groundbreaking Virtual Currency Unit identified the fraud, tracked the stolen cryptocurrency, broke new ground by uncovering the infrastructure behind the operation, and worked with the FBI to dismantle it,” Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said. 

“By disrupting more than 100 servers and hundreds of fraudulent websites, we have struck at the heart of this criminal enterprise and made it far harder for these scammers to victimize others. I commend our investigators and thank the FBI for their partnership in this extraordinary operation.”

The scam worked by luring victims via Russian-language investment ads on Facebook. A Russian-speaking “advisor” then called and walked them through opening an account on a fake crypto platform and buying digital assets. 

Weeks or months later, when victims tried to withdraw, they were locked out or hit with bogus “fees” and “taxes.” 

Some lost their life savings. Then the scammers came back for more: Posing as recovery services, they contacted victims weeks later and promised to retrieve the stolen money.

The unit had already taken down 400 scam domains, but new ones kept appearing. Hitting the servers behind them cuts off the scammers’ ability to launch new sites quickly or reach past victims.

The three-year investigation has recovered about $300,000 so far, and prosecutors say they are working to claw back more.

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Scammer loses $4.8M stored on tampered Ledgers: Asia Express
summary: A scammer reportedly lost $4.8M of stolen money after storing the funds on tampered Ledgers. Bitcoin and Ether ETFs launch trading in Thailand and South Korea blocks 27 exchanges.
content:
Major irony alert as scammer falls victim to Ledger supply chain attack

Ledger was forced to suspend its reseller network across South East Asia this week, after thieves stole more than $103.4 million from 530 addresses via tampered Ledgers inserted into the supply chain. But in a small measure of poetic justice, one of the “victims” was a scammer themselves according to Chainalysis.

The blockchain monitoring firm reports that the scammer lost 60 Bitcoin, worth about $4.8 million, from three newly purchased Ledgers containing spyware that records seed phrases. The Ledger thieves drained all three of their funds into the same wallet.

In a further irony, the scammer had operated a “task scam” where people were paid to fake sales and reviews of real items. So depending on how much they knew, their victims in turn may not have been entirely honest either. “Then a ‘negative balance’ appeared, and they were told to add their own money in order to get paid,” Chainalysis reports. So it’s possible that a scammer of scammers has just got scammed. In crypto it’s sometimes turtles all the way down.

Despite reports of tampered Ledgers showing up in Europe forcing electronics retailer MediaMarkt to suspend sales, Ledger insists that all of the confirmed thefts to date are from Asia. It has asked resellers in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong to remove Ledgers from sale. Trezor too, has decided to shutter some of the more far flung resellers in its network from Jan.1, as it can’t guarantee it can perform the same level of vigilance as it performs on resellers closer to home. There are no reports of tampered Trezors however.

In the midst of the worst hardware wallet scandal since the Coldcard seed phrase debacle at the end of July, Ledger decided it was the ideal moment to launch its latest device. Called Atom, the $849 device combines a crypto wallet with Android apps, which are kept separated from sensitive wallet operations. The device includes protections Ledger says would block the implants used in the Asian thefts and claims it can detect tampering even when switched off.

A first look at Ledger Atom. Source: Ledger

SOUTH KOREA

South Korea moves to block 27 overseas crypto exchanges

South Korean authorities have approved measures to block domestic access to 27 websites operated by unregistered crypto exchanges and other virtual asset service providers, including KuCoin, MEXC, Phemex and Bitrue. 

The Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) said in a statement: “With this decision, blocking measures against illegal virtual asset operators will also apply to internet websites, following apps such as those on Apple and Google,” the FIU said, according to a translation. 

The list also includes CoinW, BTCC, BitMart, BingX, DigiFinex and others. 

South Korea plans cybersecurity overhaul after attacks hit banks, crypto firms

South Korea will tighten cybersecurity requirements for financial institutions after an investigation into earlier security incidents involving 16 companies including crypto exchanges found some big holes. 

The Financial Services Commission said it would pursue improved threat monitoring, more frequent security assessments and stronger accountability for executives after an industry-wide review found cybersecurity deficiencies at 130 of 555 financial companies. 

South Korean bank launches Bitcoin-backed business loans: Report

Jeonbuk Bank reportedly began offering Bitcoin-backed loans to corporate customers, with a third-party custodian holding the cryptocurrency used as collateral.

THAILAND

Thailand’s Bitcoin, Ether ETFs launch trading

Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission has finalized rules that go into effect Friday allowing crypto exchange-traded funds (ETFs) to list on Thailand’s main stock exchange.

Kicking off with Bitcoin and Ether ETFs, the products must list exclusively on the Stock Exchange of Thailand. Products linked to foreign crypto ETFs will not be permitted initially, and Thai brokers are barred from facilitating investments in overseas crypto ETFs for anyone except institutions and ultra-high-net-worth individuals.

However, James Butterfill, head of research at digital asset investment firm CoinShares, told Cointelegraph not to get too excited.

“I would expect modest inflows initially, with tens of millions of US dollars across the first products a more realistic starting expectation than billions,” he said.


AUSTRALIA

Australia seeks feedback on crypto platform rules ahead of 2027 rollout

Australia’s securities regulator opened consultation Thursday on proposed capital, custody and trading requirements for crypto platforms, as it prepares to implement legislation passed in April that expands oversight of the industry. 

The proposals include three alternative capital models, restrictions on platforms trading for their own account and quarterly reporting of wallets holding customer assets. ASIC also proposes allowing offshore custody while seeking feedback on safeguards if an overseas parent or related company fails. 

The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) also proposed expanding the rules for contracts for difference (CFDs) to crypto. CFDs let traders bet on price movements without owning the underlying asset.

CHINA

Chinese fraud victims lose key court battle over 61,000 Bitcoin

Chinese fraud victims seeking to recover 61,000 Bitcoin seized by the British government have lost a key legal battle after London’s High Court ruled that Chinese law, rather than English law, should govern claims to the assets.

“The relevant damage occurred in China. The Applicants parted with their money in China,” Justice Mark Turner wrote. “The contractual relationships thereby induced were entered into in China.”

The dispute stems from an investment fraud scheme orchestrated by Zhimin Qian between 2014 and 2017, with British authorities seizing the assets during a money-laundering investigation. The claimants will appeal the ruling in British courts.

THE PHILIPPINES

Coins.ph says it still has a Philippine central bank license intact despite reports

Coins.ph said it is still licensed by the country’s central bank despite reports that it could face license revocation over alleged transactions involving restricted offshore gambling operators. 

Coins.ph is one of the largest crypto exchanges in the Philippines, and the reported license risk follows restrictions imposed by the central bank on some incoming transfers involving DCPay Philippines which operates Coins.ph’s peso e-wallet services.

“Coins.ph firmly denies any claim that it knowingly serves offshore gaming or gambling operators,” the company said. “Our users’ funds are safe; we continue to operate as a BSP-licensed institution,” it added.

HONG KONG

Binance may add Asian stocks to the platform

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said during Token2049 the exchange may add Hong Kong, Korean, Taiwanese and Brazilian equities to its platform.

Second Solana ETF lists in Hong Kong

Pando Finance’s Solana ETF has launched in Hong Kong’s HKEX under the ticker 2831.hk. It’s the second such fund and has a 0.6% fee, undercutting the first fund from ChinaAMC which charges 0.99% annually.

SINGAPORE

Singapore crypto scam losses fall by 43%

A crackdown by Singapore Police in partnership with local crypto exchanges helped contribute to a 43% fall in reported losses from crypto scams year over year.

Revolut to open new Singapore office

Revolut has announced it will open a new Singapore office, invest S$350 million (US$273M) over the next five years, and expand its local workforce from 170 to 300

title: Binance Eyes Hong Kong, South Korea, Taiwan, Brazil Stocks in Global Push
summary: Binance is exploring ways to give users exposure to leading stocks in markets including Hong Kong, South Korea, Taiwan, and Brazil as it accelerates a shift beyond crypto. Binance Moves Beyond Crypto as Exchange Model Expands Binance is looking well beyond bitcoin. The world’s largest crypto exchang...
content:
Binance is exploring ways to give users exposure to leading stocks in markets including Hong Kong, South Korea, Taiwan, and Brazil as it accelerates a shift beyond crypto.

Key Takeaways

  • Binance is exploring stock access in four markets: Hong Kong, South Korea, Taiwan, and Brazil.
  • The push extends Binance beyond crypto, fully into tokenized stocks, commodities, and pre-IPO futures.
  • Its next edge may come from combining global equities with AI-powered trading in one account.

Binance Moves Beyond Crypto as Exchange Model Expands

Binance is looking well beyond bitcoin.

The world’s largest crypto exchange is considering adding stock exposure from Hong Kong, South Korea, Taiwan, and Brazil, co-CEO Richard Teng said, as the company responds to users seeking broader access to traditional markets.

“A lot of users tell us: ‘I want access to the top stocks in Hong Kong, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil…'” Teng wrote on X. “So we’re listening, and exploring how to expand stock access across more global markets.”

The plan is still exploratory. But it fits a much larger shift underway across the crypto exchange industry.

Binance Is Building an All-in-One Trading Platform

Binance has already expanded well beyond spot crypto trading.

In 2026, the exchange introduced tokenized U.S. stocks, which recently surpassed $1 billion in assets under management (AUM) in roughly four months, making it the first tokenized equity product to hit that milestone.

Teng described the diversification as a way of “weatherproofing” the business. That strategy matters as crypto prices remain well below their 2025 peaks, putting pressure on transaction-driven exchange revenues.

Rivals are moving in the same direction. Coinbase has added stocks, perpetual futures and prediction markets as part of its “everything exchange” strategy, while OKX is developing tokenized U.S. equities through a venture with New York Stock Exchange owner, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).

Tokenized Stocks Could Open Markets Across Borders

For Binance, the pitch is also about financial access.

Teng argues tokenization and ’round-the-clock trading could give investors outside major financial centers easier access to international equities, particularly in emerging markets where brokerage access can remain limited.

That opportunity is potentially significant. A 2025 World Bank report estimated that roughly 1.3 billion adults remain without formal bank accounts.

Crypto platforms already serve many users for savings, payments, and cross-border transfers. Adding equities could make those platforms increasingly resemble global financial supermarkets.

AI Trading Adds Another Layer

Binance has also added another layer to its expansion with the launch of Binance AI Pro, an AI-powered trading assistant designed to automate market analysis, strategy execution, and position management.

Teng expects AI agents to play a larger role as investors become more comfortable delegating decisions within predefined limits.

The direction is becoming clear.

Crypto exchanges once competed mainly on coins and fees. Now Binance, Coinbase, and OKX are competing over who can offer the widest financial universe from a single account.

If Binance ultimately adds major Asian and Latin American equities, then that race will move far beyond crypto.

title: ChangeNOW Announces NOW AI After Resolving Website Integration Vulnerability
summary: Kingstown, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, 15th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Kingstown, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, 15th October 2026, Chainwire

Kingstown, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, October 15th, 2026, Chainwire

On October 15, with the help of independent security researchers, we found a vulnerability affecting one of the integrations used on the ChangeNOW website. The vulnerability has now been fixed.

We currently have no evidence that it was exploited. But we also can’t assume that the researchers who reported it were the only ones to find it. Because of that, we’re looking at the different possible scenarios and warning clients about the information that could potentially have been exposed. This may include email addresses and transaction details.

Please note ChangeNOW’s transaction infrastructure was not affected, and customer funds were never at risk.

The main thing clients should watch out for now is suspicious or fraudulent messages. A phony message could reference real transactions or support to appear legitimate. If you get an unexpected message that looks like it’s from ChangeNOW, please check the sender before responding, clicking on any links or giving any information. We exclusively contact clients via [email protected] and we will never ask for a private key, seed phrase, or any password by email.

People contact our support and compliance teams because they trust us with information they would not share publicly, and we understand the responsibility that comes with that. We have no indication this vulnerability was exploited, but we believe it is important to warn of the possible risks rather than wait until there is total certainty.

Our clients are at the center of what we do, and we’re continuing to upgrade the protection of our products. One of the actions we are taking is the launch of NOW AI, a dedicated protection lab with a mission to raise the security standard across all ChangeNOW products. We want to apply the same technology to the defensive side to spot danger earlier and bake stronger security into our products, especially as AI makes malicious action easier to automate and expand.

Today’s case only made the need to move faster more obvious and it accelerated the launch of NOW AI. We’ll publish more details on our plans, what it covers, and how it will be used across ChangeNOW on a dedicated page on our website soon. Stay tuned.

About ChangeNOW

ChangeNOW.io is a crypto super app built for every crypto move, giving newcomers, professionals, and businesses the tools they need to access Web3 finance in a simple and secure way.

Since 2017, ChangeNOW has grown from a fast, secure, and limitless instant exchange into a trusted platform where storage, swaps, trading, staking, and asset management are covered in one simple experience for millions of clients worldwide.

title: Orbs – DeFi’s Next Big Users Are Banks and Bots
summary: Ran Hammer is CEO at Orbs, a decentralized Layer-3 blockchain that works behind the scenes for DEXs. It gives smart contracts the automation and execution logic they lack on their own, which powers limit orders, TWAP, liquidity aggregation and perpetual futures across dozens of venues. Ran is an Isr...
content:
Skip to content

Ran Hammer is CEO at Orbs, a decentralized Layer-3 blockchain that works behind the scenes for DEXs. It gives smart contracts the automation and execution logic they lack on their own, which powers limit orders, TWAP, liquidity aggregation and perpetual futures across dozens of venues. Ran is an Israeli based in London and a former high-tech M&A lawyer. He has been with Orbs since its 2017 beginnings, working as general counsel, then in business development, then as chief business officer, before taking over as CEO in September.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

Ran came to crypto the way many lawyers of his generation did. In 2015 a university friend and future Orbs co-founder, Daniel Peled, told him he had raised money for his startup in Bitcoin. Within two years Ran was the rare attorney at a reputable firm who understood the technology, and he spent the 2017 ICO boom advising clients who wanted to do things by the book when no book existed yet. Nine years into Orbs, he explains plainly what the project is: a proof-of-stake network with no TVL or DEXs of its own, which supplies the automation and logic that smart contracts can’t perform by themselves. That makes Orbs nearly invisible to the traders who use it. Ran is candid that this is good for users and difficult for a project whose token benefits from retail recognition. He also acknowledges that the market has moved enough that a small pivot is needed for Orbs to stay relevant.

His view of the current market is sober. The yield chasing of DeFi summer has mostly gone. Many retail traders left after the October 10, 2025 liquidation cascade and did not return. The activity that remains is increasingly professional, ranging from two-person trading teams running bots to BlackRock buying spot assets for its ETFs, which is why Ran prefers the term “on-chain finance.” He calls Hyperliquid the most successful dApp to date. He also argues that most DEXs, even ones that dominate their ecosystems, cannot build Hyperliquid-level order book depth. Orbs’ answer is Perpetual Hub Ultra 2.0, an intent-based model in which hedgers take the other side of trades and offset them across Binance, Hyperliquid, Lighter, Variational, Aster and other venues. Users get pairs from all of those markets on whatever chain they’re on, with a single collateral. QuickSwap has already made it the default perps engine across its chains.

Ran says he rarely opens Google or Gmail anymore. He runs most of his online life through a Telegram bot on OpenClaw, with Anthropic and OpenAI models working in loops. That habit led Orbs to repackage its products as an MCP and an agent skill, and to think seriously about how a protocol gets discovered when an AI agent, rather than a person, chooses which tools to use. He says the Orbs swap skill now outranks bigger, better-funded projects on adoption, while noting that actual agentic trading volume is still smaller than the hype suggests. He also covers the recently passed OIP-9 DAO vote, upcoming Season 1 tokenomics built on revenue-funded buybacks and burns, and record staking levels despite a token he openly says is underpriced. In the hot take round, Ran calls himself 80 percent Bitcoin maximalist. He predicts that within ten years banks will provide liquidity and trade through AMMs instead of OTC desks, and says most people still underestimate what today’s AI tools can do.

title: Canton Enters South Korea as Meritz Eyes Tokenized Finance Deals
summary: South Korean investment firm Meritz Securities has struck a partnership with the Canton Foundation to explore bringing tokenized Korean financial assets into international institutional markets. The announcement shared with Bitcoin.com News explains that the agreement targets domestic securities, cr...
content:
South Korean investment firm Meritz Securities has struck a partnership with the Canton Foundation to explore bringing tokenized Korean financial assets into international institutional markets. The announcement shared with Bitcoin.com News explains that the agreement targets domestic securities, cross-border liquidity, and blockchain-based collateral.

Key Takeaways

  • Canton Foundation and Meritz Securities signed an MoU on Oct. 15 to explore tokenization in Korea.
  • Meritz Securities will examine tokenized debt, institutional collateral and cross-border liquidity.
  • Canton Network’s ecosystem includes over 1,000 institutions and 62 major Super Validators.

Canton Network Sets Sights on Korean Capital Markets With Meritz Securities Deal

Wall Street’s blockchain ambitions are finding another foothold in Asia. On Thursday, Oct. 15, the Canton Foundation announced a partnership with South Korea’s Meritz Securities. The release disclosed to Bitcoin.com’s newsdesk details that the goal is to explore tokenizing traditional financial assets and connecting them with international markets.

The arrangement also opens the door to using digital representations of high-quality debt instruments as collateral across borders. It’s an ambitious proposition, particularly in a market where evolving securities regulations will determine just how far the two organizations can take their plans.

From Korean Securities to Global Collateral

The memorandum of understanding (MoU) establishes three areas of cooperation, beginning with converting domestic financial assets into blockchain-based tokens under Korea’s developing regulatory framework. The partners will also examine Canton’s privacy-enabled infrastructure for institutional financial transactions and investigate cross-border applications involving tokenized sovereign-grade debt.

That last component carries particular financial significance. High-quality liquid assets, including certain government securities, are widely used as collateral in traditional finance (TradFi). Tokenization of real-world assets (RWAs), the foundation noted, offers a potential mechanism for transferring and coordinating those assets across participating financial platforms. However, the announcement describes exploratory initiatives rather than completed transactions or operational products.

Canton Adds Another Institutional Partner

Developed by Digital Asset, Canton operates as a public blockchain designed to accommodate institutional privacy requirements. Its broader ecosystem reportedly includes more than 1,000 institutions, with 62 major organizations serving as Super Validators.

Meritz Securities brings substantial financial backing to the arrangement. The South Korean investment firm reported 8.35 trillion won in standalone shareholders’ equity as of June 2026, ranking fourth domestically by that measure. The TradFi firm was founded in 1973, and today it commands around KRW 65-73 trillion, which is equivalent to $48.3 to $54.3 billion.

“Our collaboration with the Canton Foundation lays the groundwork for exploring how Korea’s capital markets can be linked with global digital asset infrastructure,” said Byungha Kang, managing director of Meritz Securities’ Strategic Planning Unit.

The announcement follows Tuesday’s disclosure involving S&P Dow Jones Indices, Kaiko, Derivnex, DRW, and Marex, which completed a privately negotiated total return swap on Canton using a tokenized benchmark.

Unlike that executed transaction, the Meritz agreement outlines potential applications awaiting further development. Its practical reach will depend heavily on Korea’s regulatory decisions and whether institutional participants eventually put the proposed infrastructure to work.

title: Bitcoin’s Volatility Has Fallen Within S&P 500 Ranks, Study Shows
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin’s Volatility Has Fallen Within S&P 500 Ranks, Study Shows
Grayscale research shows that bitcoin’s realized volatility is in the same range as a number of S&P 500 stocks. 
This post Bitcoin’s Volatility Has Fallen Within S&P 500 Ranks, Study Shows first appeared on Bitcoin M...
content:
Stocks and shares are a safer bet than buying bitcoin? Not so fast. 

According to research from crypto asset manager Grayscale, the digital coin’s realized volatility fell within the distribution of S&P 500 constituents — with a meaningful number of large-cap stocks exhibiting more price swings. 

Bitcoin’s price surged in August and September, giving it its best quarter in years and leading a number of analysts to declare that it’s back in a bull market. 

“As the asset has matured, with deeper liquidity, broader institutional participation, and more regulated access venues, its price swings have narrowed considerably from the extremes of its early years,” the Grayscale’s head of research, Zach Pandl, wrote in a Wednesday note. 

“That shifts the question from whether to own a volatile asset to how to size an allocation.”

He added that bitcoin’s volatility has declined to 43% over the past year, from an average of 64% over the past 10 years and 81% five years ago. 

It is now lower than that of 19% of S&P 500 constituents. “For those comfortable owning volatile equities, Bitcoin’s price fluctuations may be less daunting than assumed,” the report added. 

December data from K33 Research revealed that 2025 was the least volatile year for the asset so far. 

Bitcoin’s price became notorious for wild swings in its early days — with drawdowns of over 80% in the space of months. 

But as more investors have piled into the asset — especially since the 2024 approval of U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds — it’s become harder to move its price. 

Still, bitcoin at one point in 2026 was down over 50% from the all-time high it hit last October . It has since recovered and was recently trading for $82,485 — 35% below its record of $126,080. 

The coin in August benefited from news that the U.S. Treasury would at least double the size of its liquidity-support buyback operations. The so-called debasement trade — where investors buy an asset to hedge against a weakening currency — has become popular again, especially as the dollar has dropped. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Interactive Brokers Raises Dividend 71% as Net Interest Income Offsets Trading Slowdown
summary:
Interactive Brokers’ net interest income rose in the third quarter as larger client balances outweighed lower yields. The gain more than offset a sequential decline in commission revenue, lifting net revenue slightly above its second-quarter level. 
Separately, the board raised the quarterly dividen...
content:
2026-10-15T22:30:01.378+02:00

Thursday, 15/10/2026 | 20:30 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Interactive Brokers’ third-quarter net revenue increased 16% as larger client balances supported commission and interest income.
  • Net interest income grew despite lower yields, while trading activity declined from the exceptionally strong second quarter.

Interactive Brokers’ net interest income rose in the third quarter as larger client balances outweighed lower yields. The gain more than offset a sequential decline in commission revenue, lifting net revenue slightly above its second-quarter level.

Separately, the board raised the quarterly dividend by 71%. On an adjusted basis, net revenue reached $1.87 billion, pretax income was $1.45 billion and diluted earnings were $0.67 per share. The adjusted pretax margin narrowed to 78% from 79% a year earlier.

MetricQ3 2026Q3 2025Change
Net revenue$1.914B$1.655B+16%
Commission revenue$602M$537M+12%
Net interest income$1.154B$967M+19%
Pretax income$1.496B$1.312B+14%
Diluted EPS$0.69$0.59+17%

On an adjusted basis, net revenue reached $1.87 billion, while pretax income came in at $1.45 billion and diluted earnings were $0.67 per share. The adjusted pretax margin narrowed to 78% from 79%.

Larger Balances Offset Lower Interest Margins

Average customer margin loans reached $104.0 billion during the quarter, an increase of 47% from $70.8 billion a year earlier. Average customer credit balances rose 25% to $176.6 billion.

The expansion in balances lifted net interest income even as the profitability of those assets declined. Interactive Brokers’ net interest margin narrowed to 1.99% from 2.16% year over year.

The annualised yield on customer margin loans fell to 4.25% from 4.60%, while the yield on segregated cash and securities decreased to 3.40% from 3.81%. The figures indicate that growth came from the volume of client funds and borrowing rather than higher rates.

Trading Activity Falls from Second-Quarter Levels

Total DARTs averaged 4.27 million during the quarter. That was 18% higher than a year earlier but 11% below the second quarter. Commission revenue consequently declined from $673 million in Q2 to $602 million.

Compared with the previous year, customer futures volume increased 13%, while stock and options volumes fell 24% and 1%, respectively. Average commission per cleared commissionable order declined 4% to $2.59.

Higher regulatory charges also contributed to the annual increase in commission revenue. Execution, clearing and distribution expenses rose 46% to $134 million, largely because of a $30 million increase in regulatory fees following a higher SEC Section 31 transaction fee rate.

Interactive Brokers passes those fees through to customers.

The broker finished September with 5.58 million customer accounts and $964.7 billion in customer equity, representing annual increases of 35% and 27%, respectively.

Interactive Brokers’ board increased the quarterly dividend from $0.0875 to $0.15 per share. The dividend is payable on December 14 to shareholders of record on December 1.

title: Binance.US seeks $1B valuation in potential $100M funding round: Report
summary: The crypto exchange was reportedly looking to use the additional funding to regain market share following Binance’s 2023 settlement with US authorities.
content:
Binance.US is reportedly seeking to raise up to $100 million in a funding round that could value the cryptocurrency exchange at $1 billion.

According to a Thursday Bloomberg report, the US-based crypto exchange is pursuing private investment as it looks to expand its business. The potential $1 billion valuation would be well below the $4.5 billion pre-money valuation it secured in 2022, when it raised $200 million in seed funding.

Binance.US reportedly informed World Liberty Financial, the crypto platform co-founded by US President Donald Trump and his sons, about the funding round, but the company will not be participating. Last year, Binance was embroiled in a controversial $2 billion investment between an entity tied to the United Arab Emirates royalty and World Liberty using the platform’s USD1 stablecoin.

The proposed funding round is reportedly part of Binance.US’ efforts to regain market share against larger rivals following a 2023 settlement between Binance Holdings Ltd. and US authorities. As part of the agreement, Binance Holdings agreed to pay $4.3 billion in penalties and accept additional monitoring and oversight, while its then-CEO, Changpeng Zhao, pleaded guilty to a felony charge. Zhao completed a four-month sentence in prison before receiving a pardon from Trump in 2025.

Related: Binance says employees questioned in UAE cleared and released

title: Solana’s Alpenglow Upgrade Arrives Oct. 21 With a Major Speed Boost
summary: Earlier this week, the Solana-focused research and development firm Anza revealed that Solana’s highly anticipated upgrade Alpenglow is scheduled to activate on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. According to developers and Solana documentation, Alpenglow is expected to make finality roughly 99% faster. Sola...
content:
Earlier this week, the Solana-focused research and development firm Anza revealed that Solana’s highly anticipated upgrade Alpenglow is scheduled to activate on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. According to developers and Solana documentation, Alpenglow is expected to make finality roughly 99% faster.

Key Takeaways

  • Solana’s biggest consensus overhaul is set for Oct. 21, with Alpenglow promising to cut transaction finality from 12.8 seconds to just 150 milliseconds.
  • The upgrade replaces Solana’s existing voting system with Votor, allowing validators to reach agreements much faster without putting every vote onchain.
  • Despite the excitement surrounding Alpenglow, SOL is trading near $106, down 10% over two weeks and nearly 64% below its all-time high.

Solana Prepares for Its Biggest Consensus Overhaul

“It’s time,” Anza wrote on the social media platform X. “Alpenglow goes live on mainnet-beta Wednesday, October 21, ~14:50 UTC. 18 months of work for a migration that happens in one slot. Finality drops from seconds to ~150ms.”

Bitcoin.com News reported on the upgrade in March, explaining how Alpenglow will be Solana’s largest consensus redesign. At press time, the chain takes around 12.8 seconds to finalize a transaction, known as “finality” in blockchain spaces. When the upgrade is complete, Solana is expected to make finality a whole lot faster, to around 150 milliseconds, or 0.15 seconds.

The Layer 1 (L1) project started testnet implementations last month and Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko told the public, “You are not ready for this.” Currently, the L1 leverages a scheme called TowerBFT to help its validators agree on transactions. Under the existing design, validators submit votes through the blockchain itself. This takes time and uses network capacity.

Votor Replaces Onchain Voting With Faster Validator Consensus

Documentation covering the Alpenglow roadmap indicates that the upgrade will introduce a replacement called Votor. Instead of placing all those votes on the blockchain, validators can communicate directly with one another. Essentially, their votes will then be combined into smaller records that confirm an agreement. It’s akin to replacing a lengthy approval process with a much faster electronic vote.

The latest announcement has not bolstered SOL’s price, as Solana’s native token has shed 10% over the last two weeks. Year-to-date statistics show a near 15% decline, and SOL is still down roughly 64% below its $293 all-time high recorded in January 2025.

As of today, Oct. 15, 2026, SOL is exchanging hands for about $106, and it has gained a percentage point over the last day.

An 18-Minute Transition and an 82% Staking Threshold

As far as the upgrade is concerned, Solana will not immediately switch everything over. Instead, the network will continue using its existing system for approximately 18 minutes. During that period, blocks will contain validator votes rather than ordinary user transactions. This gives operators a controlled period to prepare for the change. Solana has explained that once the validator set reaches at least 82% of staked SOL, the L1 will switch to Votor.

Alongside this, Alpenglow has two major components, but only Votor is scheduled for Oct. 21. The second part of the upgrade will be what’s called Rotor, a design that will change how new blocks are distributed among validators. Its purpose is to make that communication process simpler and more efficient. At the time of writing, Rotor does not yet have an activation date. For now, the L1 Solana is concentrating on replacing its consensus system, the mechanism that allows the network to agree on which transactions are final.

title: Google Touts ‘Magic’ Quantum Breakthrough as Bitcoin Q-Day Threat Looms
summary: Google has announced a major quantum computing breakthrough, demonstrating a technique that reduces errors by a factor of 40 and could help make powerful quantum computers more practical. The advance comes as researchers increasingly warn that future quantum machines could undermine the cryptography...
content:
Google has announced a major quantum computing breakthrough, demonstrating a technique that reduces errors by a factor of 40 and could help make powerful quantum computers more practical. The advance comes as researchers increasingly warn that future quantum machines could undermine the cryptography securing bitcoin and other digital assets.

Key Takeaways

  • Google researchers achieved a 40-fold reduction in errors, advancing the development of powerful quantum computers.
  • Future quantum computers could potentially crack bitcoin’s cryptography, threatening wallets with exposed public keys.
  • Researchers are exploring quantum-resistant protections, but upgrading the Bitcoin network presents significant technical and coordination challenges.

Google’s Latest Quantum Breakthrough

Google Quantum AI said Thursday that researchers successfully demonstrated a technique called “magic state cultivation” on the company’s Willow quantum processor, overcoming a longstanding obstacle to developing large-scale, error-corrected quantum computers.

The research, published in the scientific journal Science, achieved a 40-fold reduction in errors compared with quantum states that had not undergone the process. Researchers also produced so-called T-states with a record logical fidelity of 99.99%, demonstrating exceptionally high accuracy in a critical component of quantum computation.

Magic states are specialized quantum resources needed to perform certain operations essential for general-purpose quantum computing. Producing them reliably has been a major engineering challenge, with some estimates suggesting that as much as 95% of a quantum computer’s capacity could be devoted to their production.

Google’s technique addresses that bottleneck by introducing a noisy quantum state into a small region of a processor and using coordinated measurements to detect errors and eliminate flawed attempts.

The researchers also demonstrated a method for transferring purified quantum states between different error-correction architectures, an important capability for scaling quantum systems.

Although Google acknowledged that significant technical challenges remain, the company described the findings as a crucial step toward building useful, fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of solving problems beyond the reach of conventional machines.

Bitcoin’s Quantum Security Threat

The breakthrough adds to growing concerns about the eventual vulnerability of bitcoin’s cryptographic security to quantum computing, an expected milestone known as “Q-Day.”

In March, Google researchers published a separate analysis suggesting that breaking the elliptic-curve cryptography underlying bitcoin’s digital signatures could require fewer than 500,000 physical qubits, approximately 20 times fewer than some earlier estimates.

That research also outlined a theoretical scenario in which sufficiently advanced quantum computers could derive a bitcoin private key from an exposed public key in roughly nine minutes, potentially allowing attackers to intercept transactions before confirmation.

Researchers estimated that approximately 6.9 million BTC could face exposure through publicly revealed keys, including older wallet formats and addresses that have been reused.

However, no quantum computer currently exists that is capable of carrying out such attacks. Google’s latest magic state research does not demonstrate an ability to break Bitcoin’s cryptography, but it addresses one of the technical obstacles to developing machines that might eventually do so.

In September, Fidelity Digital Assets warned that sufficiently powerful quantum computers could eventually derive private keys from exposed Bitcoin public keys. The firm examined quantum-resistant signature systems, including a proposed approach called SHRINCS, while highlighting the complications posed by larger signatures that could reduce Bitcoin’s transaction throughput and increase fees.

The Challenge Ahead

Just this week, crypto exchange Coinbase published a detailed assessment outlining the challenges of transitioning Bitcoin to quantum-resistant cryptography.

The exchange, which says it safeguards approximately 15% of Bitcoin’s supply, emphasized that replacing existing signature algorithms would be only one part of the solution. Developers must also consider institutional custody systems, limited blockchain capacity, compatibility with existing wallets, and funds held in dormant addresses.

Coinbase pointed to proposals, including BIP-360, as potential foundations for introducing more adaptable cryptographic protections.

A particularly difficult question concerns bitcoin held in wallets whose owners have lost their private keys or are otherwise unable to migrate their funds to new security standards. Such holdings could remain exposed even after the network adopts quantum-resistant protections.

Google has separately targeted 2029 for migrating its own systems toward post-quantum cryptography, underscoring the broader industry’s preparations.

For Bitcoin, the challenge is not an immediate security failure, but the potentially lengthy process of coordinating upgrades across a decentralized network—before quantum computers become powerful enough to threaten its existing protections.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, a Wall Street Journal investigation revealed that former Trump crypto adviser Bo Hines retained a financial stake in a firm that benefited from a Tether deal while he helped advance US stablecoin legislation. Meanwhile, Ledger introduced an $849 hardware wallet with stronger anti-tampering protections following a security incident in Asia, and Australia’s securities regulator proposed new capital, custody and trading requirements for crypto platforms ahead of a 2027 rollout.

Former Trump adviser retained stake in firm that benefited from stablecoin law

Former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines retained a one-third stake in an investment firm that received millions of dollars from Tether while he was helping advance landmark US stablecoin legislation, according to a Wall Street Journal investigation.

The report found that Nxum, an investment company Hines co-founded, received $6.3 million through an agreement with Tether, with the first payment arriving while Hines was still serving in the Trump administration.

Hines reportedly remained in contact with Nxum partners through Signal, sharing updates on the GENIUS Act and encouraging them to criticize Republican lawmakers who opposed the legislation.

The GENIUS Act, which established a federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins, was signed into law in July 2025. Hines left the administration shortly afterward, joining Tether as a strategic adviser in August before becoming CEO of its US operations.

The revelations add to scrutiny of financial ties between Trump administration officials and the cryptocurrency industry. Several former regulators have also moved into senior industry positions, including former CFTC Commissioner Summer Mersinger, who became CEO of the Blockchain Association.

Ledger’s answer to wallet tampering costs $849 and ships next year

Ledger unveiled a new device on Thursday with stronger protections against tampering, days after confirming that wallets sold through a reseller in Asia contained malicious implants.

The French hardware wallet maker introduced Atom, an $849 device that combines a crypto wallet with everyday apps through a smartphone-like design. Atom separates Android apps from sensitive wallet operations and includes protections Ledger says would block the implants used in the recent Asia incident. It’s also advertised to detect tampering even when switched off.

The company expects to begin shipping the device in summer 2027, according to an announcement shared with Cointelegraph.

Ledger said Atom will also support AI agent approvals, encrypted messaging and post-quantum cryptography.

The announcement follows a security incident that surfaced on Friday involving malicious implants found in wallets sold through authorized reseller CryptoBilis. Ledger has requested that distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong suspend sales of its products. European retail chain MediaMarkt has also pulled Ledger wallets off its shelves.

Australia seeks feedback on crypto platform rules ahead of 2027 rollout

Australia’s securities regulator opened consultation Thursday on proposed capital, custody and trading requirements for crypto platforms, as it prepares to implement legislation passed in April that expands oversight of the industry. 

The proposals include three alternative capital models, restrictions on platforms trading for their own account and quarterly reporting of wallets holding customer assets. ASIC also proposes allowing offshore custody while seeking feedback on safeguards if an overseas parent or related company fails. 

“Our proposed guidance and standards acknowledge the increasing role of digital assets and tokenization, including in traditional parts of the financial system,” said ASIC Commissioner Alan Kirkland. 

The proposed guidance and standards would give crypto operators greater clarity on requirements to obtain a license, safeguard customer assets and meet financial requirements under the new framework. The consultation follows Parliament’s passage of the Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act earlier this year.

title: 8 US States Sue OpenAI Over ChatGPT Risks as Nvidia CEO Threatens to Cut Off Unsafe AI Builders
summary: Eight U.S. states have sued OpenAI over allegations that ChatGPT exposes children and other vulnerable users to harmful content, misleading safety assurances, and potentially dangerous advice.
content:
Skip to content

Eight U.S. states have sued OpenAI over allegations that ChatGPT exposes children and other vulnerable users to harmful content, misleading safety assurances, and potentially dangerous advice.

The legal action against OpenAI comes as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he would consider cutting off chip supplies to AI developers whose products cause harm, intensifying debate over accountability across the artificial intelligence industry.

The lawsuits, filed separately on October 14, 2026, accuse OpenAI of violating consumer protection laws and failing to adequately protect young users. Meanwhile, Huang’s remarks highlight the responsibilities of companies supplying the computing infrastructure used to develop and operate advanced AI systems. Together, the developments put AI safety, corporate oversight, and consumer protection under renewed scrutiny.

OpenAI accused of prioritising profits over AI safety

Arizona, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska, and West Virginia filed the lawsuits in state courts, alleging that OpenAI promoted ChatGPT as a safe and useful tool without adequately addressing its potential risks. The complaints argue that the company’s efforts to make its chatbot engaging and agreeable may expose vulnerable users to harmful interactions.

Eight U.S. states sued OpenAI on October 14, 2026, alleging ChatGPT misrepresented its safety and exposed children to harmful advice, self-harm encouragement, and dangerous behaviors. Source: Open Source Intel via X

The allegations include claims that ChatGPT reinforced delusions, provided dangerous medical advice, encouraged self-harm, and helped users contemplate violence. Iowa’s lawsuit also alleges that the chatbot presented itself as compassionate while interacting with people in vulnerable situations. These claims have not been established in court, and the cases will determine whether OpenAI violated applicable laws.

The states are seeking civil penalties and court-ordered changes to ChatGPT’s design and operation. Some complaints call for restrictions on advanced AI model testing until appropriate safeguards are demonstrated. The requested remedies vary by state but reflect a broader effort to hold AI companies accountable for potential consumer harm.

The litigation also adds to existing legal challenges involving OpenAI. Families in separate wrongful-death cases have alleged that ChatGPT contributed to serious harm involving their relatives. Those allegations remain subject to legal proceedings and should not be treated as proof of corporate liability.

Arizona’s complaint raises a wider question about whether commercial incentives can conflict with an AI developer’s responsibility to protect users. The outcome could help clarify how existing consumer protection laws apply to AI chatbots, particularly when their conversational design may influence users’ decisions or encourage emotional dependence.

States raise concerns over children’s data and access

Several complaints focus on how ChatGPT interacts with minors and handles their personal information. The states argue that young users require stronger protections against harmful conversations, inappropriate advice, and features that may encourage excessive engagement.

Arizona’s lawsuit alleges that ChatGPT sometimes encourages teenagers to share personal information while discouraging them from discussing certain matters with parents, friends, or authorities. If substantiated, such conduct could raise concerns about privacy, parental oversight, and the boundaries between an AI assistant and a trusted human relationship.

Eight U.S. states sued OpenAI in state courts, alleging ChatGPT encouraged minors toward self-harm and violence, provided dangerous medical advice, and misled users about its safety. Source: Wealth Signal via X

The states are also seeking measures to strengthen age verification and parental controls. Other requested remedies include deleting personal information allegedly collected unlawfully from minors and requiring additional safeguards before certain AI systems can be tested or deployed.

The legal action reflects growing pressure on technology companies to demonstrate that child-safety protections work in practice, rather than relying solely on published policies. However, the specific obligations OpenAI may face will depend on the evidence, applicable state laws, and decisions by the courts.

The lawsuits also arrive amid wider disputes over responsibility for AI-related harm. Legal questions include whether companies can be held accountable for how their systems respond to individual users, what warnings consumers should receive, and whether existing laws adequately address the risks posed by generative AI.

OpenAI defends its safety measures

OpenAI has said that ChatGPT already includes protections for younger users and that it will continue improving its safeguards. The company has also expressed willingness to work with state officials on policies that can be applied across the AI industry.

OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company was committed to “advancing pragmatic AI policies that apply to the entire AI industry—not just one company,” according to The Associated Press.

The company says ChatGPT is intended for users aged 13 and older and that those under 18 need permission from a parent or guardian. It has also pointed to safeguards designed to reduce teenagers’ exposure to self-harm, violence, eating disorders, and explicit or graphic material.

OpenAI says its safety measures include break reminders for extended use and reviews involving outside experts. The company has also said that most teenagers use ChatGPT for learning, information, skill development, or productivity, with average daily usage below 15 minutes.

Those assurances will now face greater scrutiny as the lawsuits proceed. The central issue is whether existing safeguards adequately address the risks identified by state officials and whether the company’s public statements about safety accurately reflect the experience of users.

The legal challenge could also influence how AI companies approach product testing, age verification, and the handling of sensitive user information. Any broader effect will depend on the remedies sought by individual states and the eventual outcomes of the cases.

Nvidia CEO says he would cut off buyers who build unsafe AI

While OpenAI faces legal pressure over user safety, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has said his company would consider stopping chip supplies to a customer developing unsafe AI software. His comments, made in a Bloomberg interview with Emily Chang in London on October 14, highlight the potential role of infrastructure providers in AI governance.

NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang said he would consider cutting chip supplies to AI developers whose technology harms people, potentially affecting customers such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Source: Rosalie via X

Asked whether Nvidia would stop supplying an irresponsible AI developer, Huang replied: “It’s a hypothetical, but yes.”

He immediately qualified the statement, saying Nvidia would first speak with the customer. “We don’t run other people’s companies, and there’s a limit to the judgment we apply to other companies’ use of our technology. Our technology is general-purpose,” he said.

Nvidia is a central supplier of AI accelerators, specialized chips used to train and operate large AI models. Its position gives the company significant influence over the infrastructure supporting AI development, although its products can be used for a wide range of applications.

Huang did not announce a decision to suspend supplies to OpenAI, Anthropic, or any other named developer. His remarks were hypothetical and did not establish a formal policy with specific criteria for determining when an AI system is unsafe.

The Nvidia chief also pushed back against what he considers excessive alarm about AI risks, describing safety concerns as part of the growing pains of a rapidly expanding industry. Rather than slowing development, he argued that companies should accelerate the creation of tools that can contain and monitor AI systems.

“We should accelerate the integration of this containment technology into AI systems,” Huang said. He also called for faster development of monitoring technologies, arguing that AI itself could help monitor and control the technology.

Nvidia has separately pledged $250 million over five years in support of British AI safety research, with assistance taking the form of access to advanced computing resources. Researchers at institutions including the University of Oxford and University College London are expected to study safeguards and methods for controlling AI agents.

Huang’s position reflects a distinction between supplying general-purpose computing technology and taking responsibility for how customers deploy it. His comments suggest that direct engagement with customers would precede any decision to cut off supplies while leaving open questions about the standards that would trigger such action.

The developments involving OpenAI and Nvidia illustrate two different points of pressure on the AI industry. State lawsuits seek legal remedies for alleged harms to users, while Huang’s comments raise the prospect of commercial consequences for developers that fail to address safety concerns.

Neither development establishes a final standard for responsible AI development. However, the cases could help shape discussions about child protection, data privacy, model testing, and the responsibilities of companies across the AI supply chain. As AI systems become more widely used, regulators and technology providers face increasing pressure to show how safety commitments translate into effective protections.
