title: Binance Claims Fastest $1 Billion Sprint in bStocks With $6 Billion in Share Conversions
summary:
Binance has reported that its bStocks product crossed $1 billion in assets faster than any competing tokenised equity offering. 
Underpinned by $6 billion in two-way conversions with underlying shares, the product reflects growing appetite to deploy conventional equity holdings across blockchain eco...
content:
2026-10-15T20:53:29.087+02:00

Thursday, 15/10/2026 | 18:53 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Eligible Binance clients can convert supported stock positions into bStocks, trade them around the clock and use selected tokens as collateral.
  • bStocks have generated more than $40 billion in cumulative trading volume since launch.

Binance has reported that its bStocks product crossed $1 billion in assets faster than any competing tokenised equity offering.

Underpinned by $6 billion in two-way conversions with underlying shares, the product reflects growing appetite to deploy conventional equity holdings across blockchain ecosystem.

Since the June 11 launch, bStocks have generated more than $40 billion in cumulative trading volume, according to Binance’s announcement. The range has grown from five securities to almost 100 stocks and ETFs.

bStocks AUM: $1,000,000,000+ ✔️ With 1:1 convertibility and zero conversion fees, users have converted over $6B between bStocks and underlying stocks. The momentum goes beyond holding. Users are converting, trading, and building with tokenized stocks. https://t.co/Nmzou8tKzq

— Binance (@binance) October 15, 2026

How Shares Move On-Chain

Binance began offering eligible clients direct access to more than 7,000 US stocks and ETFs in early June. The service is provided by ADGM-regulated broker-dealer Nest Trading Limited, with clients holding a beneficial interest in the shares they buy.

bStocks add a second format for selected securities. A client can convert a conventional stock position into a corresponding token at a 1:1 ratio without a conversion fee, then convert it back into a direct stock position.

Each bStock is issued by Binance affiliate BTech Holdings and backed by the relevant security held with a custodian. Under the product’s terms, the token is a certificate representing an interest in that security, not direct ownership of the share.

What Clients Do with the Token

Once converted, bStocks can trade around the clock and be withdrawn to a compatible BNB Smart Chain wallet. Clients can move equity-linked exposure into self-custody or use supported tokens in decentralised finance without first selling the position for cash or cryptocurrency.

The platform added another use in September, when it extended collateral support for selected bStocks to eligible users of its Cross Margin and Portfolio Margin accounts. Clients can keep equity-linked exposure while using those tokens to support other trading positions, rather than selling them to free up collateral.

Binance’s usage figures indicate that trading outside conventional market hours is part of the appeal. Only 38% of bStocks volume in July occurred during regular US equity trading hours.

Binance Research found that 41.5% of early bStocks users had not traded its related direct-equity or perpetual products. However, the figure describes their activity on Binance and does not establish whether they had invested in shares elsewhere.

How the Milestone Compares

Binance calls bStocks the fastest tokenised equity product to reach $1 billion in assets, citing Dune data as of October 15. The claim concerns the time taken to reach that threshold, not leadership by assets held today.

On October 14, Ondo Finance said its tokenised stocks and ETFs accounted for more than $1.3 billion in total value locked. Ondo reports that measure as TVL, while Binance calls its figure AUM, so the amounts are not a precise like-for-like ranking.

A new milestone for Ondo: $4 billion in TVL. From tokenized Treasuries to tokenized stocks, ETFs, portfolios & private markets, Ondo is expanding access with every asset class. Behind the $4 billion TVL milestone: → $1.3B+ in tokenized stocks & ETFs → #1 platform for tokenized U.S. Treasuries → 1M+ cumulative holders across products That growth reflects innovations in how tokenized assets trade, including Ondo Stocks tapping TradFi exchange liquidity through RFQ. Leading wallets and apps put that liquidity within reach, enabling permissionless transfers across Solana, Ethereum and BNB Chain. This milestone is an early sign of the scale ahead as tokenization transforms how the world accesses financial markets. Think in trillions.

— Ondo Finance (@Ondo) October 14, 2026

Ondo’s broader $4 billion TVL includes other products and should not be compared with bStocks alone. Rapid growth also does not make token trading equivalent to trading the underlying shares.

The IMF’s October report found that tokenised equity markets offer access outside conventional hours but remain less liquid and more volatile than traditional counterparts. That distinction matters most when clients trade bStocks while the shares backing them are not trading on the US market.

title: At the White House, crypto policy vacancy looms large
summary: The departure of President Donald Trump's crypto adviser, Patrick Witt, leaves the digital assets office vacant and its policy aims uncertain.
content:
Oct 15, 2026, 2:48 p.m. EDT

4 min read

Summary

  • The exit of President Donald Trump’s crypto adviser, Patrick Witt, wasn’t a surprise, but it leaves the White House without an explicit digital assets policy presence.
  • The White House insists that crypto is still a priority, but its recent naming of a new AI czar left crypto off the role despite its previous inclusion.

When President Donald Trump returned to the White House last year, he not only shed his earlier resistance to crypto technology but embraced the industry with the hiring of a high-profile crypto czar and the establishment of his President’s Council of Advisors for Digital Assets.

Almost two years later, that policy push seems to have gone quiet for the moment, with the departure of Patrick Witt, who had been the final crypto adviser running that office. And when the president recently ushered in a new artificial intelligence czar, the job that was once split between crypto and AI seemed to have dropped its crypto remit.

So who is minding the store for crypto policy at the White House? It's not clear, even as a handful of people on Capitol Hill continue to suggest that the final weeks of the congressional session after the November elections could still see some legislative action for the industry. The White House still has a staff of policy advisers, and Trump's administration now boasts several crypto regulatory irons in the fire at agencies such as the Securities and Exchange Commission. But no new name has been explicitly attached to Trump's in-house crypto initiatives.

A White House official told CoinDesk on Thursday that Witt's work was appreciated and wished him "the best of luck in the future endeavors." The official didn’t comment on who would be taking over.

"Crypto and Clarity Act will continue to be a priority for the president," the official said.

The White House's digital assets policy work was never a large operation, but the advisers were highly vocal at times, and their presence could put an important administrative stamp on crypto goals. The effort began several weeks before Trump returned to office in 2025, when the president-elect named David Sacks, the former PayPal executive, as his incoming AI and crypto czar.

Trump also tapped a little-known former college football player, Bo Hines, to be the first director of the digital assets advisory council — at first a one-person effort, but eventually adding a deputy. Hines quickly became the crypto face of the White House, taking constant meetings with crypto insiders and appearing on event stages. And his brief tenure of about eight months concluded with a major win for the industry in Congress: the passage of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act into law.

A White House signing and celebration ensued, in which many of the most prominent names in crypto enjoyed front-row seats. Less than two weeks later, the administration released a comprehensive crypto agenda that set out its specific plans for fostering the sector in the U.S.

Having helped establish the U.S. law for stablecoin issuers, Hines took a job running the U.S. arm of the leading issuer, Tether. Meanwhile, a consulting firm he set up with his father and another partner, Nxum, was also paid millions of dollars as the main provider of services for a new political action committee, first revealed in reporting by CoinDesk. The super PAC was funded mostly by Tether's U.S. financial partner, Cantor Fitzgerald, and led by a Tether exec.

This week, the Wall Street Journal reported that Hines' Nxum, had received payments from Tether for consulting services while Hines was at the White House working on the GENIUS Act.

Hines' deputy on the council, Witt, took over for Hines as its new executive director. Another former football star, Witt also had a greater depth of Washington experience, and he became the face of the White House's push for the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. Over the ensuing months of negotiations, Witt didn't conceal his frustration, regularly taking to social media site X to fume about those he saw as getting in the way of the Senate bill that would erect a U.S. regulatory scaffold for crypto markets.

During that legislative process, Sacks stepped down from the czar role in March, leaving Witt and his deputy, Harry Jung, trying to manage the administration's crypto stance. That was complicated by the fact that President Trump's own crypto empire figured prominently in the talks, as Democrats demanded that senior government officials be blocked from personal crypto ties.

As the negotiations dragged further into the year — and closer to the elections — the White House offered some concessions that would have applied unprecedented ethics constraints on the president's digital assets involvement, though Democrats concluded that the agreement didn't go far enough.

Witt had confirmed in July that he had military-service commitments on the horizon with the Georgia National Guard, but he stayed to complete Clarity Act negotiations, even as his deputy left to join Hines’ Nxum. The legislation slammed into a political roadblock a month ago, failing to advance in a Senate floor vote before the chamber dispersed for a lengthy break leading up to next month's elections.

Following rumors this week that Witt had already exited, he posted Wednesday night at around midnight to confirm his departure. He thanked agency chiefs and lawmakers that had helped with Clarity, saying that "with regulators and elected officials like you, I rest easy knowing the future of digital asset innovation in America is bright." He said he'd be moving into the private sector.

Crypto insiders say they aren't sure who they'll be dealing with as their market-structure hopes have largely fizzled for the moment.

When Trump moved earlier this month to re-establish an AI overseer, hiring former SEC Chairman and current intelligence director Jay Clayton to lead his Super Intelligence Force, the job no longer mentions a crypto element. While AI and crypto enjoy some overlapping territory, Clayton comes with a rocky crypto history, having been the SEC chief that first began its stance that would be labeled "regulation by enforcement."

title: US Hoovers up Bitcoin While the World Runs on Its Digital Dollars: Report
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

US Hoovers up Bitcoin While the World Runs on Its Digital Dollars: Report
Chainalysis research shows that the U.S. is HODLing hard. 
This post US Hoovers up Bitcoin While the World Runs on Its Digital Dollars: Report first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Sa...
content:
America is accumulating bitcoin while exporting dollar-pegged stablecoins to everyone else, according to a new Chainalysis report. 

The blockchain data said in its Wednesday report, “North America: Inside the Growth of Agentic Commerce,” that the U.S. became a net importer of Bitcoin in 2026 — for the first time since 2022.

According to the data, institutions this year have been buying bitcoin while retail largely sells. 

“A dollar stablecoin is a way to hold dollars without an American bank account, and Americans already have one,” the report read. 

“The rest of the world is pivoting to a digital dollar because it meets a need that American users don’t share. Meanwhile, Americans are leaning harder on bitcoin as an infinitely scarce store of value.”

It added that U.S. dominance keeps climbing: Since the 2024 launch of spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds, America’s share of global Bitcoin activity has risen every single reporting period — even as the overall U.S. crypto economy ($2.78 trillion) contracted 2.2% in a brutal bear market, retaining most of 2025’s near-doubling.

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approved bitcoin ETFs in January 2024 after a decade of denying the products. 

Managed by Wall Street titans like BlackRock, Fidelity, and most recently, Morgan Stanley, the funds had the most successful debut in the history of ETFs. 

Institutions and Wall Street can now buy shares of the funds which track the price of bitcoin and take care of buying and selling the digital coin. 

The approval of the ETFs has helped the industry mature, the report noted, and helped the U.S. become an overall bigger bitcoin investor. 

Stablecoins, meanwhile, have turned U.S. debt into a “currency-of-choice for peer-to-peer economies as well as businesses working across borders,” the report continued. 

“In the 2026 period we continued to see stablecoins enter new use cases most especially abroad, benefitting the U.S. companies, and the U.S. government, with billions of dollars in economic activity,” it added. 

Since Donald Trump became president, he has signed a number of pro-crypto laws and executive orders. The GENIUS Act, signed in 2025, allows banks and other entities to issue stablecoins if they back the tokens with assets like U.S. Treasuries and provide monthly disclosures of their reserves.

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Ex-Trump crypto adviser profited after helping pass stablecoin bill: WSJ
summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that a company co-founded by Bo Hines benefited from the passage of the GENIUS stablecoin bill.
content:
Bo Hines, previously a crypto adviser to US President Donald Trump who later joined stablecoin issuer Tether, reportedly kept a stake in a company that profited from the passage of a stablecoin bill when he was still at the White House.

According to a Wednesday report from The Wall Street Journal, Hines had a one-third stake in the investment company he co-founded, Nxum, while pushing US lawmakers to pass the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins, or GENIUS, Act. The legislation reportedly came amid Nxum receiving $6.3 million as part of a deal with stablecoin issuer Tether, behind the USDt (USDT) token, with the first payment going through while Hines was still serving in government.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Hines kept in contact with his partners at Nxum, updating them on progress with the GENIUS Act through the Signal app while serving as Trump’s crypto adviser.

He also reportedly pressed the Nxum partners to label any Republican lawmakers opposing the stablecoin bill as “undermining the president” and “bought and paid for by democratic shills like Coinbase and a16z.” Hines joined Tether as a “strategic adviser” in August 2025, becoming CEO of its US arm the following month.

The reported deal between a former White House official and a crypto company continues to shine a spotlight on accusations that Trump and his family and staff are personally benefitting from laws they help to draft and pass. The president disclosed earning $1.4 billion from investments tied to digital assets in 2025, which included millions of dollars from his family’s crypto company World Liberty Financial, behind the issuance of the USD1 stablecoin.

Related: EU lawmakers push crypto onto anti-corruption agenda

The GENIUS Act passed Congress and was signed into law in July 2025 in a ceremony attended by many cryptocurrency executives, including those behind stablecoins like Tether and Circle. Hines was in attendance and personally recognized by Trump at the event.

Though it was signed into law in 2025, the GENIUS stablecoin bill requires rules from government agencies overseeing the tokens, including the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, Federal Reserve Board and Treasury Department. The law is scheduled to go into effect in January 2027.

Cointelegraph reached out to Tether for comment on the accusations in the report but did not receive an immediate response.

‘Revolving door’ of US policymakers to crypto companies continues

Several figures previously in government have left to become executives or advisers to digital asset companies. In addition to Hines joining Tether, Summer Mersinger, a former commissioner with the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), resigned her position three years before her term was scheduled to end for a position as CEO of the crypto advocacy group Blockchain Association. 

On Wednesday, Solidus Labs announced that Kevin Webb, a former CFTC senior counsel and adviser to former Commissioner Brian Quintenz, would join the fintech company as its vice president of policy. Webb isn’t the first former commissioner at the company, as the CFTC’s Dawn Stump left the agency in 2022 to join Solidus as a “strategic adviser.”

title: Ripple Prime Connects Institutions to Hyperliquid’s 24/7 Markets Through Swaps
summary:
Ripple Prime has begun offering institutional clients swaps linked to more than 100 traditional-asset perpetual markets. 
The underlying contracts trade on Hyperliquid, but clients enter the swaps with Ripple Prime as their counterparty and can manage them alongside other positions held through the ...
content:
2026-10-15T19:02:00.000+02:00

Thursday, 15/10/2026 | 17:02 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Institutional clients can manage round-the-clock exposure alongside other Ripple Prime positions and cross-margin eligible trades.
  • Ripple Prime is the client’s counterparty; Trade.xyz provides the reference markets on Hyperliquid.

Ripple Prime has begun offering institutional clients swaps linked to more than 100 traditional-asset perpetual markets.

The underlying contracts trade on Hyperliquid, but clients enter the swaps with Ripple Prime as their counterparty and can manage them alongside other positions held through the prime broker.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The launch comes as perpetual contracts tied to stocks, commodities and other traditional assets attract more trading activity. Open interest across several major venues has risen from almost nothing to about $9 billion over the past year, Bloomberg reported.

In February 2025, Ripple acquired multi-asset prime broker Hidden Road and renamed it Rpple Prime. The acquisition gave it access to Hyperliquid for on-chain derivatives, while the new product extends that connection to markets referencing traditional assets.

What Institutions Actually Trade

Institutions do not trade the Trade.xyz futures directly through this service. Instead, they enter swaps with Ripple Prime, which acts as their counterparty.

The swaps follow perpetual futures listed by Trade.xyz on Hyperliquid, giving clients exposure to movements in traditional assets without ownership of those assets.

That exposure can be managed outside conventional market hours because the referenced futures trade around the clock. And since they have no fixed expiry, a desk can maintain a position without rolling it into a new contract.

title: Sweden revisits digital krona as ECB advances digital euro plans
summary: Sweden’s Riksbank has recommended that lawmakers prepare for a possible digital krona, citing concerns over foreign-currency stablecoins and the future of domestic payments.
content:
Sweden’s central bank is revisiting the possibility of introducing a digital krona, citing the European Central Bank’s (ECB) progress toward a digital euro and the growing use of stablecoins as reasons to reconsider a central bank digital currency (CBDC).

In an Oct. 7 letter to parliament’s Finance Committee, published Thursday, the Riksbank urged lawmakers to begin preparing legislation for a potential digital krona, three years after a government inquiry concluded there was insufficient need for one.

The letter pointed to the ECB’s planned digital euro pilot in 2027 and a potential public launch in 2029. According to the Riksbank, Sweden’s payment system could become less competitive without a comparable digital version of its own currency.

The central bank also identified the growing use of foreign-currency stablecoins, particularly those pegged to the US dollar, as a longer-term concern, though it sees the near-term risk as limited.

“If stablecoins pegged to foreign currencies are considered attractive as a means of payment, the use of the Swedish krona could come under pressure even within Sweden’s borders,” the letter read.

The Riksbank estimates that introducing a digital krona would take at least five years, excluding the time required for legislative changes. For this reason, it recommends beginning legal preparations now, even if Sweden ultimately decides against launching a CBDC.

title: Ledger Says Organized Crime Group Spent Millions Targeting Hardware Wallet Users
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Ledger Says Organized Crime Group Spent Millions Targeting Hardware Wallet Users
Hardware wallet manufacturer Ledger has released a statement following a “sophisticated” supply chain attack. 
This post Ledger Says Organized Crime Group Spent Millions Targeting Hardware Wallet Users...
content:
Ledger has issued a statement following reports from customers of loss of funds and tampered devices, calling it one the most “sophisticated attacks” the digital asset industry has experienced. 

The hardware manufacturer said Thursday that a “highly organized criminal group” bought Ledger devices and installed implants that could read users’ seedphrases before then putting them back into the supply chain via resellers. 

Paris-based Ledger last week said it had started an investigation after customers in South East Asia reported they’d lost funds after buying from Malaysia-based reseller, CryptoBilis. 

The company then said it confirmed that one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant. 

It isn’t clear how much money has been lost from the tampered devices but blockchain investigator Specter said $86 million had been drained. Ledger did not respond to Bitcoin Magazine’s written questions. 

“[The criminal group] built their own logistics and technology infrastructure with seeds collector servers, draining and laundering infrastructures. They were patient, they spent millions, and they struck in one coordinated operation, draining wallets,” Ledger said in a Thursday statement. 

“There was no flaw in Ledger’s chip, operating system or servers. Ledger’s systems were not compromised. This was an attack on the distribution channel after the devices left our control.”

The company said that in its “largest investigation to date” it sent employees to other markets — including Europe — to make sure other supply chains hadn’t been targeted. 

It said that screened devices were clean and authorized resellers and distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong have suspended their sales. 

Ledger added that it was working with law enforcement to “follow the funds and dismantle the attackers’ infrastructure.”

It isn’t clear how many customers had been targeted from Ledger’s statement. 

The crypto industry is still reeling after hackers in July were able to steal close to $120 million in bitcoin from Coldcard users.  

There have also been a number of data breaches this year, with scammers targeting Ledger to get customer information via the company’s payment processor Global-e.

title: Bitcoin Briefly Slides Below $80,000 On More Hot Inflation Data
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Briefly Slides Below $80,000 On More Hot Inflation Data
Bitcoin has recovered slightly despite its price getting hit again by hotter-than-expected inflation data. 
This post Bitcoin Briefly Slides Below $80,000 On More Hot Inflation Data first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine a...
content:
Bitcoin’s price momentarily dipped below $80,000 on Thursday following more hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data. 

The price of the biggest cryptocurrency recently stood at $81,028 after dropping as low as $79,805 on Thursday morning in New York. 

Over a 24-hour period, it’s only down over 1% after making a recovery. But over the past week, it’s shed nearly 3% of its value. 

Data Thursday from the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics showed U.S. producer prices rose in September at the fastest pace in more than four years.

The numbers came one day after September’s Consumer Price Index came out higher than expected. 

Bitcoin has news that high prices won’t go away in the world’s largest economy — leading traders to bet that the Federal Reserve may keep interest rates higher for longer. 

The Federal Reserve will make a decision on what to do with interest rates at the end of this month. 

Bitcoin’s price has previously done well in a low interest rate environment as when borrowing costs are cut, more liquidity can be used to buy the cryptocurrency. 

But the Fed this year has raised interest rates, with the head of the central bank claiming that getting inflation down in the U.S. is its number one priority. 

The biggest cryptocurrency is currently nearly 36% below the record of $126,080 it touched last October. 

Despite the dip this week, analysts have declared the asset to be out of the bear market it spent most of 2026 following a rally in August and September. 

Mathew Di Salvo

title: Mastercard brings stablecoin balances into traditional banking and card payments
summary: The launch of Global Money Platform marks Mastercard’s first major integration with BVNK since its August acquisition, with Nuvei and Marqeta among the first companies to adopt the platform.
content:
Mastercard is expanding its role in stablecoin payments with a new platform that lets businesses integrate digital currencies into traditional banking and card services, a move that could make it easier for companies to offer stablecoin payments without building their own infrastructure.

The service, dubbed Global Money Platform, is Mastercard’s first major integration with BVNK since it acquired the stablecoin infrastructure company in August, the payments giant announced Thursday. 

According to Mastercard, businesses can use the platform to hold and convert fiat currencies and stablecoins, offer stablecoin-linked cards and make payments directly from stablecoin balances into recipients’ local bank accounts.

The service connects to Mastercard Move, the company’s global money transfer network, which can route payments to more than 17 billion destinations, including bank accounts and cards. It also connects stablecoin balances to Mastercard’s merchant network, allowing customers to spend them with payment cards. Nuvei, Marqeta and several other fintech companies are among the first integration partners.

The launch extends Mastercard’s role beyond processing payments to providing infrastructure that financial companies can use to offer stablecoin services under their own brands. It also puts Mastercard in closer competition with Visa, which launched a platform in July that lets financial institutions hold, mint, and transfer stablecoins.

It comes as research from Standard Chartered points to growing stablecoin transaction activity, even as the circulating supplies of major tokens such as USDt and USDC have remained relatively flat this year.

title: MFSA Bans Trive Shareholder for 10 Years, Freezes Client Transactions
summary:
The Malta Financial
Services Authority has barred Trive shareholder Kasim Garipoglu from taking new
positions requiring its approval for 10 years and ordered him to divest his
shareholding in the broker within six months. 
The regulator also
ordered Trive Financial Services Europe Limited to stop al...
content:
2026-10-15T17:07:05.222+02:00

Thursday, 15/10/2026 | 15:07 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The FCA also banned Kasim Garipoglu over a lack of “honesty and integrity” and deliberately misleading regulators.
  • Garipoglu must divest his qualifying Trive shareholding within six months under the MFSA’s decision.

The Malta Financial Services Authority has barred Trive shareholder Kasim Garipoglu from taking new positions requiring its approval for 10 years and ordered him to divest his shareholding in the broker within six months.

The regulator also ordered Trive Financial Services Europe Limited to stop all incoming and outgoing transactions from client accounts, citing deficiencies in safeguarding client assets and reconciliation procedures.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The MFSA ruled that Garipoglu was no longer fit and proper to hold positions requiring its approval. The order covers qualifying shareholdings he holds directly or indirectly in Trive. He must divest those holdings as soon as possible and within six months of the decision.

The MFSA’s action followed a decision by the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority to ban Garipoglu from working in UK financial services. The FCA found that he lacked “honesty and integrity” and had deliberately provided false and misleading information to the FCA and other regulators.

MFSA Orders Trive to Address Client Asset Deficiencies

The MFSA’s restrictions on Trive began in September, when the regulator ordered the firm to stop onboarding new clients until deficiencies in safeguarding client assets and reconciliation procedures had been adequately addressed.

The regulator also required Trive’s board to approve and sign off on transactions involving designated client accounts or clients’ money and assets, with appropriate oversight and supervisory controls.

Trive was instructed to provide documentation confirming that client money held by liquidity providers was maintained in the relevant accounts. The MFSA also ordered the firm to prioritise transferring client money held with counterparties to those meeting regulatory requirements.

Client Transaction Freeze Remains Until Compliance

On 24 September, the regulator imposed a further restriction, ordering Trive to stop all incoming and outgoing transactions from client accounts with immediate effect. The restriction will remain in place until the firm transfers client money to counterparties that meet the requirements or the MFSA decides otherwise.

The MFSA’s notice does not specify the amount of client money affected or state that any funds are missing.

The regulator said its decisions may be appealed before the Financial Services Tribunal within the period prescribed by law.

title: Crypto for Advisors: Wall Street is done waiting on Congress for crypto rules
content:
Oct 15, 2026, 11:00 a.m. EDT

4 min read

Summary

Happy Thursday, advisors!

In today’s newsletter, Eric Soufer of Tusk Strategies looks at what financial firms are building while Congress stalls on a crypto framework.

Then, in “Ask an Expert,” Diego Grassano explains what advisors should check before trusting a tokenized platform.

Happy reading.

- Sarah Morton

While Congress stalls, Wall Street sets its own crypto rule

Without a federal framework, financial firms are standardizing compliance and infrastructure on their own.

When the Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act on Sept. 15, the U.S. was once again left without a comprehensive federal framework for digital assets, and regulators moved to fill part of the gap. Two days later, the SEC issued an “innovation exemption” allowing certain venues to trade tokenized U.S.-listed stocks onchain.

But an exemption is not a statute, and it can be narrowed or withdrawn as easily as it was granted. That leaves financial firms with a practical question: What do you build while you wait? For advisors, the answer matters more than who won or lost in Washington.

That question ran through a Crain’s New York Business event last week, whether the topic was tokenization, compliance or cybersecurity. The people closest to the work aren’t waiting for Congress. They’re building for the world as it is.

Adam Schumann, vice president of legal at OKX, laid out the legal problem. U.S. firms answer to federal statutes, federal agencies, state laws and state regulators, and none of them move at the same speed. “You want general consistency, but you’re not going to reach uniformity,” he said. Firms work out the rest state by state and country by country, while agencies patch the most immediate gaps.

That patchwork has a cost. Aravind Raju, CFO of Uphold, said compliance is now one of the company’s largest departments because it builds tailored solutions for each state’s requirements. As rules become clearer and more aligned, he expects those resources can be redirected. For advisors, the takeaway is that compliance is a real cost of doing business on these platforms, and the firms that manage it well will have an edge.

You might expect that duplication to push the industry toward shared infrastructure. Instead, many institutions launched private, closed networks this year for tokenized assets, stablecoins and securities ledgers, and those networks can’t easily talk to one another. Lewis Tuff, CEO of Twilight, which builds clearing and settlement technology, said the result is that every firm ends up rebuilding the same connections.

Risk is moving in the opposite direction, toward separation. Early crypto firms bundled trading, custody and clearing under one roof. Today, traditional custodians hold digital assets, and the venues that execute trades are increasingly separate from the ones that safeguard them. That means no single entity has to hold every key function or become a single point of failure. Compliance and security are shifting too, from annual attestations and periodic reviews to checks that run continuously, with every transaction.

None of this required Congress, and that’s the point. Without a comprehensive framework, the industry is converging on practices any future law would find hard to ignore: verified counterparties, clear lines between trading and custody, and compliance that never stops running.

Whether these practices become a bridge to legislation or a substitute for it is still an open question, but the direction is clear. Raju offered one prediction. Within three years, he said, “we’ll probably stop using the word ‘crypto’ as tokenized Treasuries and money funds become routine.”

If he’s right, the infrastructure being built now, without a statute to guide it, will matter well beyond this cycle.

- Eric Soufer, partner and head of advanced tech, Tusk Strategies

Ask an Expert

Q. Regulatory Vulnerability: How risky is it for institutions to pour capital into infrastructure built on temporary SEC exemptions and state-level workarounds?

The main risk is committing long-term capital to infrastructure that may only have temporary permission to operate. Exemptions can help institutions get started, but they need a credible plan if those permissions change or expire. I’d want clear ownership rights, segregated custody and a tested exit route that allows investors to recover their assets.

Q. Solving Fragmentation: How can institutions bridge siloed, private blockchains without compromising security or regulatory isolation?

Institutions need to connect networks without losing control over ownership, compliance or privacy. Bridges are improving but still carry real security and operational risks. While regulatory standards remain fragmented, I’d keep the legally recognized ownership record on the original chain and allow backed, redeemable representations to circulate elsewhere, with eligibility and transfer restrictions enforced on both networks.

Q. Actionable Advisor Takeaways: What criteria should financial advisors use to vet tokenized platforms when federal investor protections are still in limbo?

I would start with two questions: What does my client actually own, and how do they get their money back? Then check who holds the assets, who independently verifies the numbers and what happens if the platform fails. Look closely at fees, conflicts and withdrawal restrictions. If an advisor cannot clearly explain the ownership structure, the risks and the recovery process to a client, the due diligence is not finished.

title: Schwab Trading Activity Jumps 44%, Outpacing Revenue Growth
summary:
Charles Schwab’s daily trade count rose 44% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, while trading revenue increased 16%. The gap left the brokerage earning less revenue per reported trade even as its wider business posted record quarterly revenue.
London's trading industry is coming home!
Clien...
content:
2026-10-15T16:29:31.821+02:00

Thursday, 15/10/2026 | 14:29 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Schwab’s revenue per reported trade fell 20% year over year to $1.69, despite higher trading revenue.
  • Net interest and asset management and administration fees generated about three-quarters of the group’s quarterly revenue.

Charles Schwab’s daily trade count rose 44% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, while trading revenue increased 16%. The gap left the brokerage earning less revenue per reported trade even as its wider business posted record quarterly revenue.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Clients completed an average of 10.7 million trades per day, up from 7.4 million a year earlier. Trading revenue rose from $995 million to $1.158 billion, according to Schwab’s results.

Revenue per Trade Falls from a Year Earlier

Charles Schwab reported revenue per trade of $1.69, down 20% from $2.11 in the third quarter of 2025. The sequential comparison was different: daily average trades fell 10% from the second quarter, while trading revenue declined about 5%. Revenue per trade consequently rose from $1.64 in Q2.

Schwab divides trading revenue by all reported trades, including commission-free stock and ETF orders and trades allocated by investment advisers. Options trades, by contrast, carry a $0.65 per-contract fee.

It is not the commission paid on a typical order: the trade count also includes commission-free transactions and trades made under asset-based pricing arrangements.

Trading revenue itself combines commissions, payments for order flow and principal transactions, according to Schwab’s filings.

These activities generate revenue in different ways. The third-quarter release does not break out their contributions, so the figures do not establish what caused the year-on-year decline in revenue per trade.

Trading Is One Part of Schwab’s Growth

Charles Schwab’s two largest revenue categories continued to grow. Net interest revenue increased 14% to $3.476 billion, while asset management and administration fees rose by the same percentage to $1.913 billion. Total net revenue reached $7.171 billion, up 17%, and net income increased 23% to $2.906 billion.

The company also attracted $190.4 billion in core net new assets during the quarter, 38% more than a year earlier. Total client assets reached $13.33 trillion, and clients opened 1.2 million new brokerage accounts.

Client balances matter to Schwab beyond trading: uninvested cash helps fund interest-earning assets, while funds and managed investments generate ongoing fees.

Despite the sharp rise in trade count, trading supplied about 16% of Schwab’s quarterly net revenue. Net interest and asset management and administration fees together accounted for approximately 75%.

VIENNA, October 15, 2026 – BingX EU (MEGE zweite GmbH) has secured its Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA or MiCAR) license from Austria’s Financial Market Authority (FMA), that will enable the platform to offer regulated crypto services across 29 countries of the European Economic Area (EEA), subject to ongoing passporting arrangements. The authorization marks a significant milestone in BingX’s European expansion, providing EEA users with access to digital asset services under a unified regulatory framework built on transparency, security, and investor protection.

The authorization reflects BingX EU’s long-term commitment to responsible growth in Europe. As digital assets become increasingly integrated into the financial system, regulatory clarity plays an essential role in strengthening user confidence, supporting institutional participation, and enabling sustainable industry development. Through its regulated European entity, BingX EU will provide compliant crypto services designed to meet the evolving needs of both retail and institutional users across the EEA.

“Our priority is to provide European users with trusted and locally regulated trading experience,” said Daniel Lai, Chief Executive Officer of BingX EU. “Operating under MiCAR will allow us to deliver our services under a clear regulatory framework that gives users confidence while supporting the long-term development of Europe’s digital ecosystem. It also enables us to combine innovation with the high standards of security, transparency and accountability that European users and institutions expect. We believe this foundation can help create a more accessible and sustainable environment for the continued adoption of digital assets across the region.”

Looking forward, BingX EU will continue working closely with Austria’s FMA and other European regulators as it prepares for the launch of its regulated services across the European Economic Area. BingX EU remains committed to operating within Europe’s regulatory framework while providing users with secure, transparent and compliant access to digital asset services.

About BingX EU

MEGE zweite GmbH (“BingX EU“) is a MiCAR-regulated crypto-asset platform, headquartered in Vienna, licensed as a Crypto-Asset Service Provider (CASP) under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCAR). Dedicated to serving clients across 29 countries in the European Economic Area, BingX EU delivers fully regulated services in alignment with European standards for investor protection and market integrity. Under its MiCAR authorization, BingX EU provides a platform that offers regulated broker services, such as crypto custody, exchange, and other crypto services.

For media inquiries, please contact: media@bingx.eu

About BingX

Founded in 2018, BingX is one of the the world’s leading multi-asset trading platform, serving more than 40 million users worldwide. The company has been the Principal Partner of Chelsea FC since 2024 and became the Official Team Partner of Scuderia Ferrari HP in 2026.

content:
2026-10-15T14:52:04.277+02:00

Thursday, 15/10/2026 | 12:52 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The company is replacing CMC Connect with CMC Markets Institutional.
  • The institutional business serves banks, brokerages, family offices, hedge funds and dealing desks.

CMC Markets is rebranding its institutional business as CMC Markets Institutional, replacing the CMC Connect name as the group brings its institutional services under the main brand.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The move follows the company's expansion of its institutional and business-to-business operations. In July, CMC Markets reported record client assets of £46.3 billion. The firm also announced a trading technology partnership with Westpac in Australia to expand its customer base.

CMC Rebrand Leaves Services Unchanged

The rebranded business will cover trading, investing and wealth solutions, including multi-asset liquidity, trading technology, investment infrastructure, and access to public and private markets.

CMC Markets said the change would not affect the services available to existing institutional clients and partners.

CMC Previously Operated Separate Institutional and Retail Brands

CMC Markets introduced the CMC Markets Connect brand in January 2021 to distinguish its institutional business from its retail offering. The company said at the time that the move reflected increased investment in institutional services, including liquidity provision, pricing and execution.

The business serves banks, brokerages, family offices, hedge funds and dealing desks . Its services include multi-asset liquidity, trading technology, API connectivity and white-label solutions that allow partners to offer trading through their own platforms. The former CMC Connect website reported more than 150 institutional partners.

Prime Services Covers Equities and Financing

In May 2026, CMC Markets launched Prime Services capabilities through CMC Connect. The offering included cash and synthetic prime brokerage, financing, multi-asset execution and post-trade support.

The service provides access to cash equities, exchange-traded funds and synthetic single-stock exposure through direct market access and smart order routing.

The rebranding changes the institutional business's name but, according to CMC Markets, does not alter the services available to existing clients and partners.

title: Lynx Opens Warsaw Office With Fewer Clients Than XTB Adds in Six Weeks
summary:
Dutch broker Lynx is opening an office in Warsaw, it said today (Thursday). Poland becomes the fifth country where the Amsterdam-based company runs a local team, and it says it serves more than 72,000 active investors across Europe.
That is fewer than the Polish brokerage accounts XTB opens in six w...
content:
2026-10-15T14:42:58.140+02:00

Thursday, 15/10/2026 | 12:42 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The Dutch broker counts 72,000 active investors, and Trade Nation opened zloty accounts the same day.
  • Each newcomer targets a different part of the market leader’s business, from savings and CFDs to options.

Dutch broker Lynx is opening an office in Warsaw, it said today (Thursday). Poland becomes the fifth country where the Amsterdam-based company runs a local team, and it says it serves more than 72,000 active investors across Europe.

That is fewer than the Polish brokerage accounts XTB opens in six weeks at its August pace. XTB ended August with 1,235,335 accounts, up 53,621 in a month.

Its accounts make up more than 40% of the 3,029,784 registered with the Central Securities Depository of Poland (KDPW). The two measures differ, as KDPW counts every registered account, funded or not.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Lynx is not the only foreign broker moving on Poland, which generated 54.4% of XTB's revenue in 2025.

Trade Nation launched zloty accounts on the same day, and Trade Republic entered the country in September 2025 as its first market outside the euro zone. Each has picked a different part of XTB's business.

Lynx Goes After Active Stock Traders

Lynx has served Polish clients since 2017, according to its careers page, and now lists a Polish branch of Lynx B.V. in central Warsaw. Founded in 2006, it is supervised by the Dutch Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM) and De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).

Lynx works as an introducing broker for the Irish unit of Interactive Brokers, which executes orders and holds client assets. Interactive Brokers reported client equity of $962.8 billion in August.

Clients reach more than 100 exchanges through Lynx's own app or Interactive Brokers' Trader Workstation, with support in Polish. Lynx will also issue the PIT-8C, the annual statement Polish brokerages send clients for capital gains tax, Parkiet reported.

"We grow gradually, country by country, not everywhere at once," Lynx CEO Ellen van Ginkel said in comments published by Parkiet.

She pointed to the number of active Polish brokerage accounts, which she said had more than tripled since 2019, as the reason for a local team.

The product list includes options and futures. XTB added options to its Polish terms of service in June and already sells them in Cyprus, Germany and Spain. In July, XTB CEO Omar Arnaout called the Polish launch a matter of time.

XTB has kept adding features for the same traders. On October 7 it began rolling out 24-hour weekday trading in selected US shares to Polish clients.

Trade Nation Brings Fixed-Spread CFDs

Trade Nation's Polish service runs under its license from the Portuguese Securities Market Commission (CMVM), passported into Poland, the company said. It offers contracts for difference (CFDs) in zloty accounts with fixed spreads.

New markets include the Poland 20 index and shares of Allegro, CD Projekt, Orlen and Żabka. The London-based firm acquired FXCM's UK client book earlier this month.

"Poland has one of the most active and sophisticated trading communities in Europe," Trade Nation Chief Executive Jon Noble said.

CFDs still drive XTB's results. They generated about 96% of its result from financial instruments in the first half of 2026, even as most new clients started with stocks and ETFs.

The Polish Financial Supervision Authority (KNF) counted 369,737 active OTC derivatives clients at domestic brokerages in 2025, up 50% from a year earlier. One bank is moving the other way: mBank stopped signing new mForex agreements on September 3.

Trade Republic Took the Savings Route

Trade Republic opened in Poland with a flat trading fee of 4 zlotys and a savings account paying the central bank rate, the company said at launch. Its arrival coincided with mBank and DM BOŚ dropping commissions on ETFs held in retirement accounts.

The German firm runs its Polish business under its German banking license and offers stocks, ETFs and crypto with local IBAN accounts. In May it raised the rate on Polish cash balances to 6%, Bankier reported.

Crypto is one product XTB cannot yet sell from Poland. Arnaout said in July the company would offer it once the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) is implemented in Polish law.

The pool of idle cash is large. Poles hold more than 1 trillion zlotys in current accounts paying little or no interest, plus about 420 billion zlotys in term deposits, said Arkadiusz Jóźwiak, editor-in-chief of Polish financial news site Comparic.pl.

"There is a lot to fight for," Jóźwiak told FinanceMagnates.com.

Jóźwiak said many Polish brokerages followed XTB into commission-free trading in stocks and ETFs, and that newcomers face clients used to good terms from local and foreign firms alike.

Neither Trade Republic nor Lynx appears in the KDPW figures, which cover only domestic institutions. The same gap applies to Revolut, which reported 590,000 Polish investment accounts a year ago under its Lithuanian license.

title: How Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI took down a massive crypto fraud network targeting Russian speakers
summary: The scheme allegedly stole tens of millions through Russian-language Facebook ads and fake advisers, then went after victims again with fake recovery offers.
content:
Oct 15, 2026, 8:35 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI seized or disrupted 241 scam websites and 112 servers tied to a crypto fraud that targeted Russian speakers in the US.
  • The scheme allegedly stole tens of millions through Russian-language Facebook ads and fake advisers, then went after victims again with fake recovery offers.
  • Officials have seized about $300,000 so far. Crypto scams made up roughly 84% of the investment-fraud losses reported to the FBI in 2025.

Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI have seized or disrupted 241 websites and 112 servers tied to a crypto investment scam that allegedly stole tens of millions of dollars from Russian-speaking victims in the U.S.

The operation, carried out last week, came after a three-year investigation into a fraud network that relied on online infrastructure and IP addresses in Ukraine and other Eastern European countries, Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said. No arrests were announced.

The scammers drew victims through Russian-language Facebook ads that promised investment opportunities. Fake advisers then called the victims and coached them to buy cryptocurrency and send it to fraudulent trading platforms.

When victims tried to withdraw their funds, the platforms locked their accounts or demanded more payments for supposed taxes and fees.

The scammers then “tried to exploit them again with false promises to recover their money,” Gonzalez said. Recovered data showed they contacted victims a few weeks after the initial fraud, offering to retrieve the stolen funds.

The DA’s Virtual Currency Unit had previously seized or disrupted 400 domains tied to crypto investment fraud, but replacement sites kept appearing.

This time, investigators targeted the servers, hosted by Eastern European and U.S. companies, that held victim data and the software used to run the fraud. The goal was to stop the operators from quickly launching new sites.

The case comes as crypto investment scams accounted for roughly 84% of the $8.65 billion in investment-fraud losses reported to the FBI in 2025, according to the bureau’s annual report.

Across all internet-crime categories, crypto-linked losses totaled $11.37 billion, approximately 54% of the $20.88 billion overall. Both percentages are calculated from the FBI’s totals.

Brooklyn authorities have seized about $300,000 and are working to recover more. Prosecutors said some victims lost their entire life savings.

title: Polygon Unlocks 48-State US Payments Reach With Coinme and 4 Early OMS Customers
summary:
Key Takeaways: Polygon acquired Coinme, which expands its payments business to include coverage in the 48 U.S. states. Now it has 37 money transmitter licenses, 11 state exemptions and is
The post Polygon Unlocks 48-State US Payments Reach With Coinme and 4 Early OMS Customers appeared first on Cryp...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Polygon acquired Coinme, which expands its payments business to include coverage in the 48 U.S. states.
  • Now it has 37 money transmitter licenses, 11 state exemptions and is FinCEN registered.
  • First companies making payments, payroll and dollar access on Polygon Open Money Stack include Tazapay, Mesh, Toku & Kira.

Polygon Labs has completed its acquisition of Coinme, turning Polygon Open Money Stack into a regulated U.S. payments platform with direct links between fiat and onchain money movement.

The partnership provides Polygon with added protection and wallets, on-ramps, and cross-chain routing and settlement capabilities to shield its stablecoin payments.

  • Coinme Gives Polygon Coverage Across 48 US States
  • Stablecoins Connect More Directly to Local Currency
    • Mesh, Toku and Kira Expand Polygon’s Payments Footprint
    • Polygon Pushes Deeper Into Stablecoin Payments

Coinme Gives Polygon Coverage Across 48 US States

Coinme is Polygon’s U.S. payments service now available in 48 states, with 37 state money transmitter licenses and 11 exemptions that apply. The business is also registered as a money services business with FinCEN.

This regulatory component is being incorporated into the Polygon Open Money Stack (OMS).

It will aim to link bank accounts, cards and cash to onchain transfers, wallets and finally payouts. Businesses don’t need to stitch small transactions together from various providers; instead, they can send money into crypto rails with one stack, send money across networks, and then take it back down and make it usable as money in the real world.

Read More: Securitize Puts 12 U.S. Stocks on Solana With 1:1 Backing and 24/7 Trading Plans

Stablecoins Connect More Directly to Local Currency

Tazapay is amongst the early adopters of the OMS. It supports over 1,000 businesses and fintechs in more than 30 countries and has implemented Polygon’s on/off ramp solutions to reduce the time to market of stablecoins and local currencies.

The aim is to shorten the path for cross-border payments, without eliminating pre-existing local payment systems and SWIFT.

Mesh, Toku and Kira Expand Polygon’s Payments Footprint

Polygon OMS on-ramps will be added to the network cleared of over 300 wallets, exchanges and financial services. This integration provides alternative pathways between digital and fiat currencies without forcing companies to create numerous unique integrations.

Toku’s global payroll solutions are powered by Polygon wallets and payout systems. It handles local payroll, tax withholding and hiring compliance in over 100 countries, while also facilitating payments to employees who receive stablecoins and then use them to buy local currency.

Kira is also working to include Polygon OMS to increase the numbers of fintechs and institutional access to stablecoins. It has a platform that allows conversion to USD, ACH, Fedwire, FedNow, SWIFT and stablecoin. Kira 10 says the sign up takes only 72 hours and 9/10 payments are instant approval.

Polygon Pushes Deeper Into Stablecoin Payments

Coinme’s deal will take Polygon off the infrastructure-only business. Enabling regulated fiat entry into the application alongside on-chain settlement, wallets, and payouts, Polygon is developing one of crypto’s surging use-cases: transporting stablecoins from traditional financial systems to crypto networks.

Polygon OMS is in production now with its first customer demonstrating its ability to enable cross-border payments, account funding, payroll enrollment and access to the U.S. dollar.

title: Under pressure, Ledger unveils plan to turn its crypto hardware wallet into a smartphone
summary: Ledger’s Atom will run apps like WhatsApp and Instragram and let users switch between smartphone functions and a protected mode for managing digital assets.
content:
Updated Oct 15, 2026, 9:51 a.m. EDTPublished Oct 15, 2026, 8:00 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Ledger’s Atom, scheduled for release in mid-2027, will run apps like WhatsApp and Instragram and let users switch between smartphone functions and a protected mode for managing digital assets.
  • The device will include tamper-resistant enclosures, sensors and packaging intended to prevent supply-chain attacks like the recent CryptoBilis breach, even when switched off.
  • Ledger initially plans to sell Atom only through its website to limit third-party distribution risks, but it will not offer trade-ins for customers affected by the breach.

Cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker Ledger said it is developing a new device that looks and functions more like a smartphone than a traditional wallet.

The Ledger Atom, scheduled for release in mid-2027, marks a departure from the industry’s emphasis on safeguarding digital assets on minimalist devices meant to be locked away in a drawer or a desk.

The Atom runs Android, meaning users will be able to install everyday applications like WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok. Users can switch between ordinary smartphone functionality and a protected mode for managing digital assets. The device also incorporates integration with the AI assistant OpenClaw.

The product will be manufactured at Ledger’s location in Vietnam, as is customary with its more complex devices.

The Atom announcement comes amid fallout from a supply-chain security breach involving Malaysian distributor CryptoBilis, in which attackers reportedly tampered with devices before they reached customers. Onchain researchers estimated losses of up to $93.2 million across more than 300 wallets, with Tether freezing $10 million of its dollar-pegged stablecoin USDT tied to the theft.

The compromised wallets allegedly contained hidden chips capable of intercepting users’ 24-word recovery phrases — the stream of random words that only the owner of the wallet should know as the ultimate safeguard to their digital assets — by reading signals from their screens.

The incident largely affected users in Southeast Asia, with Ledger citing research on Wednesday to show no loss of funds reported in Europe.

Ledger says Atom will incorporate additional protections specifically designed to counter this type of attack, a spokesperson told CoinDesk via email. The safeguards include a protective enclosure around the device’s most sensitive components, sensors that detect attempts to remove its screen or back cover and packaging designed to reveal whether it has been opened.

The tamper-detection system has its own battery to ensure it functions even if the device is switched off.

“The Core protection enclosure will explicitly block the screen reader implants from this weekend’s incident,” the spokesperson said.

Ledger plans to initially sell the device exclusively through its own website rather than through third-party sellers, in theory reducing exposure to distribution channels implicated in the CryptoBilis incident.

The company also said it has no plans to introduce trade-in programs for existing customers affected by the incident, though it does not rule out future upgrade promotions.

The concept of combining smartphone functionality with hardware-level crypto security isn’t entirely new. Solana introduced its Saga smartphone in 2023, followed by its successor, Seeker, last year. Both featured built-in hardware protection for private keys. Ledger is approaching this idea from the opposite direction, by starting with a crypto security device and turning it into something resembling an everyday smartphone.

UPDATE (Oct. 15, 12:05 UTC): Adds the location of Atom’s manufacturing and references research on CryptoBilis incident not showing any loss of funds in Europe.

content:
2026-10-15T13:53:01.168+02:00

Thursday, 15/10/2026 | 11:53 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • National regulators reported 955 sanctions, and Germany, France and Spain imposed two-thirds of the money.
  • The first penalties under the EU crypto rulebook came to 10 measures and one EUR 600,000 fine in Germany.

Financial regulators across Europe imposed EUR 81.9 million (about $92 million) in administrative fines in 2025, 18% less than in 2024. The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) published the figures today (Thursday).

Its third annual sanctions report counted 955 sanctions and measures by national authorities, close to the 975 recorded a year earlier. A growing share of the money came through settlements.

London's trading industry is coming home!

For brokers and other investment firms, the money sits in a few places. Fines under MiFID II , the EU rulebook for investment firms, totaled EUR 36.6 million, and Germany, France and Cyprus accounted for 80% of that sum, according to the report.

Germany alone accounted for 61% of that money with 8% of the actions, according to an FM Intelligence analysis of the ESMA data, which found Cyprus was the only country to ban people or remove licenses under those rules.

The report lands a week after EU finance ministers agreed to move only the largest crypto firms, trading venues and clearing houses under direct ESMA supervision, leaving most enforcement with national authorities.

ESMA Asks for More Consistent Enforcement

ESMA said the report highlights "significant differences in enforcement" between countries, in the number and type of sanctions, the size of fines and the use of settlements. It called for stronger convergence where low enforcement activity cannot be explained by the size of a national market.

George Theocharides, chairman of the Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC), said in June that a single market needs a level playing field as more trading crosses borders.

"Supervisory effectiveness ultimately depends on market participants' compliance with the rules," ESMA said in a statement.

The authority said it will keep running case discussions among national supervisors so that similar breaches lead to similar outcomes.

The push will pass to new leadership on November 1, when Carlo Comporti, a commissioner at Italian markets regulator Consob, succeeds Verena Ross as ESMA chair.

Germany's Two Largest Fines Were Settled

Of EUR 83.8 million in pecuniary sanctions, which include fines and the return of illicit profits, EUR 35.6 million, or 42%, came through settlement procedures. In 2024 the share was slightly above 20%.

By number, 153 of the 955 measures were settled, or 16%, up from about 10%.

Germany imposed two fines of EUR 7.4 million each through settlement for breaches of MiFID II organizational requirements. ESMA did not name the firm or firms.

Together the pair made up 40% of MiFID II fine value across the European Economic Area (EEA). Under MiFID II as a whole, 75% of the pecuniary value was settled, compared with 35% in 2024.

Three Countries Collected Two-Thirds of the Fines

Germany imposed EUR 23.4 million in fines, France EUR 17.8 million and Spain EUR 12.5 million. Together they held 66% of the EEA total, up from 57% a year earlier.

Counts point elsewhere. Hungary imposed the most sanctions and measures, 189, of which 85 were cease-and-desist orders, followed by Italy with 111 and Czechia with 70. Lithuania imposed none.

Cyprus, home to 20% of the firms passporting investment services to other member states, reported 34 measures under MiFID II and EUR 2.6 million in fines. Those included all nine temporary bans, suspensions and withdrawals of authorization recorded under MiFID II in 2025.

FinanceMagnates.com reported last year that Cyprus-based firms served about a third of EU cross-border retail clients in 2024. ESMA's latest cross-border data, published a day before the sanctions report, put the total at about 15.5 million clients.

Ireland has issued no MiFID II sanctions since 2018. The Central Bank of Ireland told ESMA it has sanctioned firms under the earlier MiFID I rules for obligations that continue today.

First Penalties Under the Crypto Rulebook

The year brought the first sanctions under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). Authorities in Austria, Germany, Liechtenstein and the Netherlands imposed 10 measures, including one fine of EUR 600,000 in Germany and one withdrawal of authorization.

Most concerned firms offering crypto services without the required authorization. Authorized crypto-asset service providers grew from six in 2024 to 194 in May 2026, ESMA said, and a FinanceMagnates.com count of its register found 323 active entities by mid-August, 22% of them in Germany.

Cases against licensed firms fall into next year's data. In August, Austria's regulator published its first MiCA penalty order, a EUR 70,000 fine on Bitpanda over marketing and white paper breaches.

The report covers only breaches of EU acts in ESMA's remit. Anti-money laundering sanctions and penalties under purely national law are not included.

title: Bitcoin, copper, stocks, yields all fall; gold rises
summary: Your day-ahead look for Oct. 15, 2026
content:
Updated Oct 15, 2026, 7:27 a.m. EDTPublished Oct 15, 2026, 7:15 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

This is an excerpt from CoinDesk newsletter 'Daybook.' Sign up here, if you haven't already.

Bitcoin BTC$80,955.28 has dropped more than 2% in the past 24 hours, with some of the other major coins such as XRP (XRP), ether ETH$2,432.81 and solana (SOL) sliding even further. The move looks less like a crypto-specific story and more like a broad-based exit from riskier investments.

Futures tied to copper, a closely watched barometer of global economic health, fell nearly 1%, extending Wednesday's 1.6% decline. Other growth-sensitive assets tumbled, with Asian stocks dragged lower by a rout in Korean chipmakers. Nasdaq index futures and risk-sensitive currency pairs such as Aussie dollar-Swiss franc, are down as well.

At the same time, Treasury yields are falling — meaning bond prices are rising — while gold is up 1%. The yield on the 10-year note, the benchmark borrowing rate, has dropped by eight basis points to 5.08%, extending the pullback from the recent peak of 5.36%. Treasuries and gold are often treated as haven investments.

Together, the moves point to investors reducing exposure to risk and seeking safety, with some stagflation fears mixed in.

“It feels more like a stagflationary environment where risk assets and the US dollar generally underperform, while gold outperforms,” InvestingLive analyst Giuseppe Dellamotta wrote in a market update.

Concerns the Fed will raise interest rates have been cited as one catalyst after Wednesday’s hotter-than-expected U.S. CPI report. But that concern appears to be fading.

CME fed funds futures now price in only a 29% chance of the central bank hiking its benchmark rate into the 4%–4.25% range later this month. The remaining probability is for rates to stay unchanged at 3.75%–4%. Odds briefly approached 50% after the CPI print, but quickly scaled back.

Looking ahead, Thursday’s producer price index will offer another read on how much inflation remains in the pipeline. A hot number could add fuel to the risk-off mood.

Traders will also watch the AI trade and whether it continues to unwind. Analysts at 10x Research still prefer holding bitcoin while that unwind plays out, but only as long as BTC holds above $78,000. Further, they prefer to “use ether as a hedge for BTC long positions.”

Stay alert!

Read more: For analysis of today's activity in altcoins and derivatives, see Crypto Markets Today . For a comprehensive list of events this week, see CoinDesk's "Crypto Week Ahead."

What’s trending

  • BlackRock's Fink names a U.S. recession trigger, sounds alarm over $40 trillion national debt (CoinDesk): Companies are pouring so much money into the data centers that power AI that any attempt to slow it could hurt the U.S. economy, not just the stock market, said BlackRock CEO Larry Fink.
  • Bitcoin mining pool once handling 2.3% of network shuts after hashrate falls 65% (CoinDesk): Crypto exchange Binance is shutting the bitcoin mining pool it launched in April 2020.
  • Stocks slide as AI rout drives investors to bonds (Bloomberg): Global equities fell as a selloff in artificial intelligence gathered speed and pushed investors toward the safety of bonds.

Today’s signal

The chart shows ether’s daily price swings in candlestick format since May.

Ether is testing a dual support zone near $2,350, formed by a horizontal trendline and an ascending trendline. The horizontal line has acted as persistent support since Aug. 23, while the ascending trendline marks the bullish trend from the July lows.

A break below this confluence would signal a significant weakening of demand and could open the door to deeper losses.

title: Altcoins lead crypto declines as Asian stocks drop; bitcoin little changed since midnight
summary: Bitcoin fell to just above $80,000 as South Korea’s Kospi plunged 8%, while the CoinDesk 80 fell 2.2% and all but six CoinDesk 100 members declined.
content:
Updated Oct 15, 2026, 10:05 a.m. EDTPublished Oct 15, 2026, 6:52 a.m. EDT

4 min read

Summary

  • Bitcoin fell to just above $80,000 at around 02:30 UTC, close to the Oct. 8 low, before recovering to about $81,200, down around 0.5% since midnight UTC.
  • South Korea’s Kospi plunged 8% and triggered circuit breakers, while Nasdaq 100 index futures slid about 1% and the odds of an October Fed rate hike eased to roughly 26% from a spike near 47%.
  • The CoinDesk 80 slid 2.2% against 0.7% for the CoinDesk 5, and all but six CD100 members were lower.

Bitcoin BTC$82,074.35 is trading at $81,200, down around 0.5% since midnight UTC after trimming a 1% loss from earlier in the session, with buyers stepping in just above $80,000 at around 02:30 UTC, close to the Oct. 8 low of about $80,300.

Asian equities set the tone, with South Korea’s Kospi plunging 8% and triggering circuit breakers while Nasdaq 100 index futures slid about 1%, extending Wednesday’s 1.9% drop in the Nasdaq Composite.

Altcoins took the heavier losses, with ether ETH$2,432.50 down 2.0% near $2,370. The CoinDesk 80 (CD80) slid by 2.2% while the bitcoin-dominant CoinDesk 5 (CD5) lost around 0.7%.

The bigger moves were apparent across lower market cap tokens, with pump.fun PUMP$0.004509 falling by 9.4% as the CoinDesk Memecoin Index lost 4.0%, leaving all but six CD100 members lower.

The odds of an October Federal Reserve interest-rate increase jumped to nearly 47% on CME’s FedWatch after Wednesday’s hotter-than-expected inflation report, from about 22% beforehand. It’s now back to roughly 26%, which leaves Treasury yields and hike pricing as the next signals heading into the U.S. open.

Derivatives positioning

  • Liquidations jumped to nearly $1 billion after a hot inflation print: Nearly $1 billion in crypto futures bets were liquidated over 24 hours as the market wilted after Wednesday's hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation report, up from about $136 million a day earlier. The spike shows how crowded positioning was heading into the data.
  • Ether took a heavier hit than bitcoin: ETH saw more liquidations than bitcoin. Longs worth $200 million were liquidated in ether, significantly more than the $115 million in bitcoin. The difference points to heavier long leverage in ether.
  • Silver outranked a top privacy coin on liquidations: XAG (silver) perpetual futures have seen more liquidations than zcash (ZEC), one of the top privacy coins in a sign of the growing popularity of TradFi assets on crypto platforms.
  • Trading surged while open interest held steady: 24-hour crypto futures volume is $252 billion, up 61% over the period, while open interest (OI) is largely unchanged at $139.6 billion. That means the activity was mostly existing positions being closed or churned, not a big new leverage build. The taker long/short volume ratio is again skewed bearish, with shorts accounting for 51.67% of the flow, little changed from 52% a day earlier.
  • Traders are adding to bitcoin positions as the price falls: BTC's spot price is down over 2% in 24 hours, but notional futures OI is up 1.6%. Because OI is measured in dollars, that implies the number of contracts rose by roughly 3.7%, so net new capital is entering during the drop. The 24-hour OI-adjusted cumulative volume delta (CVD) is negative, alongside negative readings for most coins, so the new money looks more like shorts. OI doesn't show direction, however. BTC's perpetual funding rate is still positive, so longs are still paying to hold.
  • Ether and solana show a similar setup: ETH and SOL futures OI have held largely steady despite bigger spot price drops than bitcoin. Flat dollar OI amid falling prices implies the number of contracts rose by about the size of the price drop, another sign of fresh positions. Both also have negative CVDs and still-positive funding rates.
  • DOGE and NEAR are being de-risked: Their OI drops are far bigger than their spot price declines, which means traders are closing positions and capital is leaving, not just marking down.
  • Bitcoin's implied volatility is holding above 40%: The BVIV index is just above 40% for the second straight day, up from recent lows near 34%. The increase shows renewed demand for options, which remain well short of the panic highs seen in February and June. Ether's volatility index shows a similar pattern.
  • Options flow is two-way in bitcoin and defensive in ether: On Deribit, BTC calls at the $90K and $86K strikes top the 24-hour options volume rankings, while the other three in the top five are puts. Calls above the market point to bets on a rebound, and the puts point to hedging. In ETH's case, puts top the list.

Token talk

  • Pump.fun PUMP$0.004509, the Solana memecoin launchpad token, fell 9.4%, the steepest loss in the CD100, with the broader Solana ecosystem also taking a hit. Jito JTO$0.4551 lost 6.2% and jupiter (JUP) 6.1%, while solana (SOL) slipped only 1.1% to about $103.
  • Pyth network PYTH$0.09277, an oracle token, rose 2.8%, extending a rally that began Oct. 8 after its DAO voted to direct all product revenue into monthly buybacks. CoinMarketCap shows about $96 million of PYTH volume over 24 hours, a 67% increase on the previous 24-hour period.
  • Starknet STRK$0.08457 gained 11%, rebounding after a 17% slide on Oct. 13. It remains 278% higher than its yearly low of $0.021 on Aug. 16.
  • Canton CC$0.1064, the institutional blockchain token, fell 7.3%, optimism OP$0.1288 lost 7.0% and aerodrome (AERO) dropped 6.4%, as a lack of altcoin liquidity continues to weigh on the sector.
  • Larger names held up better, with tron TRX$0.3338 little changed, monero (XMR) down 0.55% and hyperliquid (HYPE) down 0.96% to about $80.
